knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper Subdifferential Variational Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform norm control over all Fréchet upper subgradients at a nearby approximate minimizer; the theorem does not assert nonemptiness of the upper subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be a Banach space and let $\varphi:X\to\mathbb R$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. For every $\varepsilon,\lambda>0$ and every $x_0\in X$ satisfying $\varphi(x_0)<\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon$, there exists $\bar x\in X$ such that $\|\bar x-x_0\|<\lambda$, $\varphi(\bar x)<\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon$, and $\|x^*\|<\varepsilon/\lambda$ whenever $x^*\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every strict approximate minimizer has a nearby strict approximate minimizer at which each existing Fréchet upper subgradient has norm below epsilon divided by lambda. No existence of an upper subgradient is asserted, so the universal condition may be vacuous when the upper subdifferential is empty.
assumptions_latex: \varphi:X\to\mathbb R\text{ is l.s.c. and bounded below}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar x:\ \|\bar x-x_0\|<\lambda,\quad \varphi(\bar x)<\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon,\quad \forall x^*\in\widehat\partial^+\varphi(\bar x),\ \|x^*\|<\varepsilon/\lambda.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ekeland variational principle with square-root perturbation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate-minimizer formulation on a complete metric space with perturbation and displacement parameters both equal to the square root of epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let (X,d) be a complete metric space, let f:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be lower semicontinuous, let x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f, and let \epsilon>0 satisfy
\[
f(x_0)\le\inf_{x\in X}f(x)+\epsilon.
\]
Then there exists \bar x\in X such that
\[
d(\bar x,x_0)\le\sqrt\epsilon
\]
and
\[
\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\sqrt\epsilon\,d(x,\bar x)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-minimizer of a lower semicontinuous function on a complete metric space lies within square root epsilon of a point that exactly minimizes the function after addition of a square-root-epsilon distance perturbation centered at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar x\in X:\ d(\bar x,x_0)\le\sqrt\epsilon,\quad \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\sqrt\epsilon\,d(x,\bar x)\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ekeland Variational Principle in Euclidean Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation of an approximate minimizer into the unique minimizer of a norm-penalized objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}} be lower semicontinuous with \inf f\in\mathbb{R}. If \bar x\in\varepsilon\text{-}\operatorname*{argmin}f for \varepsilon>0, then for every \delta>0 there exists \widetilde x\in\mathbb{B}(\bar x,\varepsilon/\delta) such that f(\widetilde x)\leq f(\bar x) and
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x}\{f(x)+\delta\lVert x-\widetilde x\rVert\}=\{\widetilde x\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every epsilon-minimizer of a lower-semicontinuous function with finite infimum can be moved by at most epsilon divided by delta to a no-worse point that uniquely minimizes the function after adding a delta-weighted distance penalty centered at that point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\widetilde x\in\mathbb{B}(\bar x,\varepsilon/\delta):\ f(\widetilde x)\leq f(\bar x),\quad \operatorname*{argmin}_x\{f(x)+\delta\lVert x-\widetilde x\rVert\}=\{\widetilde x\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ekeland Variational Principle and Completeness Characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-space form, including the converse characterization of completeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space. If $X$ is complete, $\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below, $\varepsilon>0$, and $\varphi(x_0)\leq\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon$, then for every $\lambda>0$ there exists $\bar x\in X$ such that $\varphi(\bar x)\leq\varphi(x_0)$, $d(\bar x,x_0)\leq\lambda$, and $\varphi(x)+(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,\bar x)>\varphi(\bar x)$ for every $x\neq\bar x$. Conversely, if for every bounded-below Lipschitz function $\varphi:X\to\mathbb R$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\bar x$ satisfying $\varphi(\bar x)\leq\inf_X\varphi+\varepsilon$ and $\varphi(x)+\varepsilon d(x,\bar x)>\varphi(\bar x)$ for all $x\neq\bar x$, then $X$ is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a complete metric space, every proper lower-semicontinuous bounded-below function and every approximate minimizer admit a nearby no-worse point that becomes a strict minimizer after adding the prescribed distance penalty. Conversely, the corresponding unit-scale property for all bounded-below Lipschitz functions characterizes completeness.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is complete},\quad \varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\text{ is proper, l.s.c., and bounded below}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar x:\ \varphi(\bar x)\leq\varphi(x_0),\ d(\bar x,x_0)\leq\lambda,\ \forall x\neq\bar x,\ \varphi(x)+(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,\bar x)>\varphi(\bar x);\text{ the stated Lipschitz property with }\lambda=1\text{ conversely implies completeness.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ekeland Variational Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric perturbation form parameterized by \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E,\rho)\) be complete and let \(f:E\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be lower semicontinuous with \(\inf_E f\in\mathbb R\). If \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(f(\bar e)\leq\inf_E f+\varepsilon\), then for every \(k>0\) there exists \(\widehat e\in E\) such that \(\rho(\bar e,\widehat e)\leq k^{-1}\), \(f(\widehat e)\leq f(\bar e)-\varepsilon k\rho(\bar e,\widehat e)\), and \(f(\widehat e)-\varepsilon k\rho(e,\widehat e)<f(e)\) for every \(e\in E\setminus\{\widehat e\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-semicontinuous function with finite infimum on a complete metric space, every epsilon-minimizer admits, for each positive k, a nearby improved point that is a strict minimizer of the corresponding distance-perturbed objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\widehat e\in E:\ \rho(\bar e,\widehat e)\leq k^{-1},\quad f(\widehat e)\leq f(\bar e)-\varepsilon k\rho(\bar e,\widehat e),\quad \forall e\neq\widehat e,\ f(\widehat e)-\varepsilon k\rho(e,\widehat e)<f(e).

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-feasible-set form of Ekeland's variational principle on the complete restricted metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(x_\varepsilon\in C\) such that
\[
f(x_\varepsilon)\le f(x_0),\qquad d(x_\varepsilon,x_0)\le\lambda,
\]
and
\[
f(x)>f(x_\varepsilon)-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,x_\varepsilon)
\quad\text{for every }x\in C\setminus\{x_\varepsilon\}.
\]
Both the selected point and all comparison points are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonempty closed feasible subset of a complete metric space, Ekeland's point remains feasible and satisfies the strict perturbed minimality inequality against every other feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is complete, \(C\subset X\) is nonempty and closed, and \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\varepsilon\in C\), \(d(x_\varepsilon,x_0)\le\lambda\), and \(f(x)>f(x_\varepsilon)-(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,x_\varepsilon)\) for every \(x\in C\setminus\{x_\varepsilon\}\).

children.title: Feasible-Neighborhood Forms
children.top_down_role: Variants combining locality with domain restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Neighborhood Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ekeland's principle on a closed feasible neighborhood, with the selected point localized inside the neighborhood radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(x_\varepsilon\in D\) such that
\[
f(x_\varepsilon)\le f(x_0),\qquad d(x_\varepsilon,x_0)\le\lambda<r,
\]
and
\[
f(x)>f(x_\varepsilon)-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,x_\varepsilon)
\quad\text{for every }x\in D\setminus\{x_\varepsilon\}.
\]
In particular, \(x_\varepsilon\in C\cap\overline B(x_0,\lambda)\), while the comparison inequality is asserted only on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a closed feasible neighborhood, Ekeland's principle gives a feasible point within the chosen localization radius, with perturbed minimality asserted against points in that neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is complete, \(C\subset X\) is closed, \(x_0\in C\), \(r>0\), and \(D=C\cap\overline B(x_0,r)\).
\(f:D\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\varepsilon\in C\cap\overline B(x_0,\lambda)\) and \(f(x)>f(x_\varepsilon)-(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,x_\varepsilon)\) for every \(x\in D\setminus\{x_\varepsilon\}\).

children.title: Boundary-Sensitive Regimes
children.top_down_role: Effects of feasible-set boundaries on localized perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a closed subset of a complete metric space and \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) satisfies the constrained Ekeland hypotheses.
\(x_\varepsilon\in C\) is the resulting Ekeland point with perturbation slope \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\nabla_C f|(x_\varepsilon)\le\alpha\), while no bound for \(|\nabla f|(x_\varepsilon)\) follows unless ambient competitors are locally feasible.

notation.meaning: strong slope computed using competitors in C
ambient strong slope when f has an ambient extension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary points yield a relative slope estimate; an ambient slope estimate requires local interior feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Subdifferential Variational Principles p. 206
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The constrained Ekeland inequality
\[
f(x)\ge f(x_\varepsilon)-\alpha d(x,x_\varepsilon)
\quad\text{for all }x\in C
\]
implies the relative strong-slope estimate \(|\nabla_C f|(x_\varepsilon)\le\alpha\). If \(x_\varepsilon\) is a boundary point of \(C\), this does not imply the corresponding ambient estimate \(|\nabla f|(x_\varepsilon)\le\alpha\), because descent directions leaving \(C\) are absent from the comparison. The ambient estimate follows when a neighborhood of \(x_\varepsilon\) is contained in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible boundary, Ekeland controls only the slope relative to feasible competitors; ambient descent can remain uncontrolled unless the selected point is locally interior.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Sensitive Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Real Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real form of Ekeland's variational principle, including indicator-function representations of constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(x_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{dom}f\) such that
\[
f(x_\varepsilon)\le f(x_0),\qquad d(x_\varepsilon,x_0)\le\lambda,
\]
and
\[
f(x)>f(x_\varepsilon)-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,x_\varepsilon)
\quad\text{for every }x\in X\setminus\{x_\varepsilon\}.
\]
If \(C\subset X\) is closed and \(g+\delta_C\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below, applying this form to \(f=g+\delta_C\) yields the corresponding constrained formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ekeland's principle applies to proper lower semicontinuous extended-real functions. A closed-set indicator encodes feasibility whenever the resulting function satisfies the theorem's hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is complete and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{dom}f\), \(d(x_\varepsilon,x_0)\le\lambda\), and \(f(x)>f(x_\varepsilon)-(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,x_\varepsilon)\) for every \(x\in X\setminus\{x_\varepsilon\}\).

Ekeland point in the effective domain

children.title: Ordered Set-Valued Extension Family
children.top_down_role: Order and set-valued extensions.

children.title: Vector-Valued Forms
children.top_down_role: Perturbational principles for vector-valued objectives.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is complete, \(Y\) is a real topological vector space, and \(K\subset Y\) is a closed convex cone.
\(e\in\operatorname{int}K\), and the scalarization \(x\mapsto\varphi_e(F(x)-y_0)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)-y_0\notin \varphi_e(F(x_*)-y_0)e-(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,x_*)e-\operatorname{int}K\) for every \(x\ne x_*\).

notation.meaning: cone scalarization defined by the displayed infimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalarization-derived vector form; stronger cone-order variants require a specified ordering convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\lambda>0\), scalar Ekeland applied to \(x\mapsto\varphi_e(F(x)-y_0)\) yields \(x_*\in X\) with \(d(x_*,x_0)\le\lambda\), \(\varphi_e(F(x_*)-y_0)\le\varphi_e(F(x_0)-y_0)\), and
\[
\varphi_e(F(x)-y_0)>
\varphi_e(F(x_*)-y_0)-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,x_*)
\]
for every \(x\ne x_*\). Equivalently, the vector \(F(x)-y_0\) cannot belong to \(\varphi_e(F(x_*)-y_0)e-(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,x_*)e-\operatorname{int}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalarizing a cone-ordered vector objective and applying Ekeland produces a nearby point satisfying a strict scalarized, and hence cone-exclusion, variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Vector-Valued Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar Ekeland conclusion is plausible, but the claimed equivalence with the displayed cone-exclusion relation depends on exact properties of the Gerstewitz scalarization and the cone convention. An authoritative source is required before fixing the vector formulation.

children.title: Set-Valued Forms
children.top_down_role: Perturbational principles for multifunction or set-valued objectives.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is complete, \(Y\) is a real topological vector space, and \(K\subset Y\) is a closed convex cone with \(e\in\operatorname{int}K\).
\(G:X\rightrightarrows Y\) has nonempty values and \(m(x):=\inf_{y\in G(x)}\varphi_e(y-y_0)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m(x)>m(x_*)-(\varepsilon/\lambda)d(x,x_*)\) for every \(x\ne x_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infimal-scalarization form for a set-valued objective; direct set-order formulations depend on additional conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\lambda>0\), Ekeland's principle applied to the scalar merit function \(m\) gives \(x_*\in X\) such that
\[
d(x_*,x_0)\le\lambda,
\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0\u00a0 m(x_*)\le m(x_0),
\]
and
\[
m(x)>m(x_*)-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,x_*)
\quad\text{for every }x\in X\setminus\{x_*\}.
\]
Thus a set-valued optimization problem admits an Ekeland point whenever its infimal cone scalarization is an admissible extended-real objective. Any direct inclusion statement for \(G(x)+K\) additionally depends on the selected set order and attainment of the inner infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued problem inherits Ekeland's conclusion when its values define a proper lower semicontinuous infimal scalarization; direct set-order conclusions need additional conventions.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Applying scalar Ekeland to the merit function is plausible, but no source supports this as the intended set-valued form. The relation to a genuine set order, inner-infimum attainment, and value closedness remains convention-dependent.

children.title: Order-Structured Extensions
children.top_down_role: Extensions governed by cones, partial orders, or preference relations.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a complete metric space and \(Y\) is a Hausdorff locally convex space ordered by a closed convex pointed cone \(K\).
\(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) has nonempty values, an appropriately closed graph, and is bounded below in the \(K\)-order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) is minimal for the distance-perturbed order and lies within \(\lambda\) of the initial approximate minimizer.

notation.meaning: Ordering cone in the range space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-ordered, set-valued Ekeland extension with a metric perturbation in a fixed positive direction.

source_refs.locator: 5.3.2 Generalized Order Optimality p. 73
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0\in X\) be an \(\varepsilon\)-approximate \(K\)-minimizer of \(F\). Under the stated order-completeness and closedness hypotheses, there exist \(\bar x\in X\) and \(\bar y\in F(\bar x)\) such that \(d(\bar x,x_0)\leq\lambda\), and for every \(x\neq\bar x\),
\[
F(x)\cap\left(\bar y-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,\bar x)k_0-K\right)=\varnothing.
\]
Thus no distinct feasible image improves upon \(\bar y\) after charging the metric displacement in the ordered direction \(k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate cone-minimizer can be localized to a nearby point that becomes minimal after adding a distance-dependent perturbation in a positive order direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Structured Extensions

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3.2 Generalized Order Optimality p. 73

The cited section must be inspected for the exact order, completeness, and closedness hypotheses.

children.title: Scalarization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Passage from ordered or set-valued problems to scalar variational forms.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a Hausdorff locally convex space and \(K\subset Y\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cone comparisons are exactly the simultaneous scalar comparisons generated by \(K^+\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone scalarization of cone comparisons used by ordered vector and set-valued variational principles.

source_refs.locator: 5.3.2 Generalized Order Optimality p. 73
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(y_1,y_2\in Y\), separation of the closed convex cone gives
\[
y_1\leq_K y_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \langle y^*,y_1\rangle\leq\langle y^*,y_2\rangle\ \text{for every }y^*\in K^+.
\]
Consequently, an ordered perturbation \(y\mapsto y+\alpha k_0\), with \(k_0\in K\) and \(\alpha\geq0\), becomes the scalar penalty \(\alpha\langle y^*,k_0\rangle\) under each \(y^*\in K^+\). Any strict scalar minimum for one normalized \(y^*\), where \(\langle y^*,k_0\rangle=1\), excludes domination detectable by that scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive dual functionals convert cone comparisons and ordered metric perturbations into scalar inequalities and scalar penalties.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalarization Interfaces

children.title: Borwein–Preiss Variational Principle
children.top_down_role: Smooth strengthened perturbation family.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space, \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nearby point is a strict minimizer after addition of a differentiable series of power-distance perturbations.

notation.meaning: Power used in the smooth perturbation
Perturbation centers converging to the minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Power-distance form of the Borwein–Preiss smooth variational principle on a Banach space.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.3 Smooth Variational Principles p. 210
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \(\bar x\in X\), points \(x_i\to\bar x\), and numbers \(\mu_i>0\) with \(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\mu_i=1\), such that \(\|\bar x-x_0\|<\lambda\), \(f(\bar x)\leq f(x_0)\), and \(\bar x\) is a strict global minimizer of
\[
x\longmapsto f(x)+\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda^p}\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\mu_i\|x-x_i\|^p.
\]
For \(p>1\), the perturbation is Fréchet differentiable at \(\bar x\) whenever the norm-power terms have the required smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A near-minimizer can be moved slightly so that a convergent weighted sum of smooth power-distance penalties makes it a strict minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Borwein–Preiss Variational Principle

children.title: Deville–Godefroy–Zizler Variational Principle
children.top_down_role: Smooth variational principle for Banach-space renorming structures.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space admitting a \(C^1\)-smooth Lipschitz bump function.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An arbitrarily small smooth Lipschitz perturbation makes \(f\) attain a strong minimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DGZ smooth variational principle in a Banach space possessing a smooth Lipschitz bump.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.3 Smooth Variational Principles p. 210
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists a bounded \(C^1\)-smooth Lipschitz function \(g:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
\|g\|_\infty<\varepsilon,
\qquad
\sup_{x\in X}\|g'(x)\|<\varepsilon,
\]
such that \(f+g\) has a strong minimum at some \(\bar x\in X\); that is, \((f+g)(x_n)\to(f+g)(\bar x)\) implies \(x_n\to\bar x\). The differentiability class of \(g\) may be raised when the available bump function has the corresponding higher smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Banach space with a smooth Lipschitz bump permits arbitrarily small smooth perturbations that force lower-semicontinuous objectives to have strong minima.
knowledge_statements.title: Deville–Godefroy–Zizler Variational Principle

children.title: Smooth-Bump Perturbation Principles
children.top_down_role: Perturbation families controlled by smooth bump functions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space with a bounded \(C^1\)-smooth Lipschitz bump.
\(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Smooth bump functions generate perturbations that are simultaneously small in value and derivative and that enforce minimization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract perturbation principle generated by smooth Lipschitz bump functions.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.3 Smooth Variational Principles p. 210
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\eta>0\), the smooth-bump perturbation mechanism produces a bounded \(C^1\)-smooth Lipschitz function \(g:X\to\mathbb R\) with
\[
\sup_{x\in X}|g(x)|<\eta,
\qquad
\sup_{x\in X}\|g'(x)\|<\eta,
\]
for which \(f+g\) attains a minimum. At any minimizer \(\bar x\), the smooth sum rule yields \(-g'(\bar x)\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)\), so the perturbation controls both objective displacement and first-order residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth bumps yield perturbations whose values and derivatives are uniformly small, while forcing a minimizer and a controlled subgradient residual.

children.title: Fuzzy Subdifferential Principles
children.top_down_role: Approximate generalized-gradient localization.

knowledge_statements.title: Fuzzy Subdifferential Principles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fuzzy Fréchet-subdifferential stationarity for a finite sum on an Asplund space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist \(x_i\in X\) and \(x_i^*\in\widehat\partial f_i(x_i)\) such that
\[
\|x_i-\bar x\|<\varepsilon,
\qquad
|f_i(x_i)-f_i(\bar x)|<\varepsilon,
\qquad
\left\|\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^*\right\|<\varepsilon.
\]
Thus exact stationarity of the sum is represented, up to an arbitrarily small residual, by subgradients evaluated at possibly different nearby points rather than necessarily at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimum of a nonsmooth sum, nearby Fréchet subgradients of the summands can be chosen so their sum is arbitrarily small.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is an Asplund space and \(f_i:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(1\leq i\leq m\), are lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(\sum_{i=1}^m f_i\), and all but at most one summand are locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nearby Fréchet subgradients of the summands can be selected with arbitrarily small sum.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global additive-gap definition of approximate minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A point \(x_\varepsilon\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-approximate global minimizer of \(f\) if
\[
f(x_\varepsilon)\leq\inf_{x\in X}f(x)+\varepsilon.
\]
For \(\varepsilon=0\), this is exact global minimization. For a nonempty feasible set \(C\subset X\), define its indicator by \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. The constrained definition is obtained by replacing \(f\) with \(f+\delta_C\), equivalently by requiring \(x_\varepsilon\in C\) and taking the infimum over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate minimizer is a feasible point whose objective value exceeds the global infimum by no more than the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty set and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and bounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\varepsilon\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-approximate minimizer exactly when its objective gap is at most \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Approximate Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Localized first-order residual behavior near candidate solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space, \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\).
\(\partial f(x)\subset X^*\) is the subdifferential selected for the ambient calculus, and \(\eta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate stationarity means that the selected subdifferential contains a dual vector of norm at most \(\eta\), up to closure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-residual definition relative to a specified generalized subdifferential.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.2 Subdifferential Variational Principles p. 206
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(x\) is \(\eta\)-stationary for \(f\), relative to \(\partial\), when
\[
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x))\leq\eta.
\]
Equivalently, \(0\in\overline{\partial f(x)+\eta B_{X^*}}\). If \(\partial f(x)\) is norm closed and the distance is attained, this reduces to the existence of \(x^*\in\partial f(x)\) satisfying \(\|x^*\|\leq\eta\). Exact stationarity corresponds to \(\eta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is approximately stationary when its generalized subdifferential comes within the chosen tolerance of the zero dual vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists \(\bar x\in X\) such that

d(\bar x,x_0)\leq\lambda,
\qquad
f(\bar x)\leq f(x_0),
\qquad
f(x)>f(\bar x)-\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,\bar x)
\quad\text{for all }x\neq\bar x.

children.title: Localization-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where near-optimality does not yield useful local stationarity.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near-optimality and vanishing first-order residual do not imply localization when compactness or coercivity is absent.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of localization without coercivity or compact sublevel sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The smooth convex function \(f(x)=e^x\) satisfies \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R}f(x)=0\), but it has no minimizer. For \(x_n=-n\),
\[
f(x_n)=e^{-n}\downarrow0,
\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x_n))=|f'(x_n)|=e^{-n}\downarrow0,
\qquad
|x_n|\to\infty.
\]
Thus the same sequence is increasingly near-optimal and approximately stationary while escaping every bounded set. A coercivity, compactness, or independent localization hypothesis is therefore necessary to infer a convergent localized subsequence from these two residuals alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the exponential function, near-minimizers have vanishing gradients but escape to minus infinity, so stationarity does not supply localization without compactness or coercivity.
knowledge_statements.title: Localization-Loss Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) such that
\[
\|x-x_0\|<\varepsilon,
\qquad
|f(x)-f(x_0)|<\varepsilon,
\qquad
\widehat\partial f(x)\neq\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, the graph of \(f\) over points admitting a Fréchet subgradient is dense in the graph of \(f\) with respect to the product topology of \(X\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-valued domain point can be approximated in both position and value by points where the Fréchet subdifferential is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.title: Density Consequences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) on a finite-dimensional normed space and any \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), the limiting subdifferential admits the representation \[\partial f(\bar x)=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{x\to\bar x,\,f(x)\to f(\bar x)}\widehat\partial f(x).\] Equivalently, \(x^*\in\partial f(\bar x)\) precisely when sequences \(x_k\to\bar x\), \(f(x_k)\to f(\bar x)\), and \(x_k^*\to x^*\) exist with \(x_k^*\in\widehat\partial f(x_k)\). Hence nearby regular approximations transfer to limiting calculus objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting subgradients are exactly limits of Fréchet subgradients taken at nearby points with convergent function values.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be complete, and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and bounded below. If \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\) satisfy \(f(x_0)\le\inf_X f+\varepsilon\), then there exists \(\bar x\in X\) such that \(d(\bar x,x_0)\le\lambda\), \(f(\bar x)\le f(x_0)\), and \[f(\bar x)<f(x)+\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}d(x,\bar x)\qquad\text{for every }x\ne\bar x.\] Thus \(\bar x\) strictly minimizes the distance-perturbed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every approximate minimizer can be moved a controlled distance to a strict minimizer of a linearly perturbed objective.

children.title: Variational Well-Posedness
children.top_down_role: Existence, uniqueness, and minimizing-sequence stability.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is variationally well-posed exactly when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_X f=\{\bar x\}\) and every sequence \((x_k)\) with \(f(x_k)\to\inf_X f\) satisfies \(x_k\to\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tikhonov well-posedness for an unconstrained metric optimization problem.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Characterizations of Well-Posedness and Sensitivity Analysis p. 377
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and bounded below. The minimization problem \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) is variationally well-posed in the Tikhonov sense when there exists a unique minimizer \(\bar x\in X\) and every minimizing sequence converges to it; explicitly, whenever \(f(x_k)\to\inf_X f\), one has \(d(x_k,\bar x)\to0\). Equivalently, the approximate solution sets \(\{x:f(x)\le\inf_X f+\varepsilon\}\) shrink to \(\bar x\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem is variationally well-posed when it has one minimizer and every sequence approaching the optimal value converges to that minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Variational Well-Posedness

children.title: Generic Stability
children.top_down_role: Stable behavior prevalent across suitable model classes.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a Baire topological space of perturbation parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is generically stable when some residual set \(G\subset P\) satisfies \(S(p)=\{x(p)\}\) for \(p\in G\), and \(p_n\to p\in G\) implies \(x(p_n)\to x(p)\) whenever \(p_n\in G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-set stability of uniquely selected minimizers within a perturbation family.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Characterizations of Well-Posedness and Sensitivity Analysis p. 377
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a Baire topological space, and let \(f_p:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be an optimization problem for each \(p\in P\), with solution mapping \(S(p):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f_p(x)\). The family is generically stable if there is a residual set \(G\subset P\) such that \(S(p)=\{x(p)\}\) for every \(p\in G\), and the selected minimizer depends continuously on the parameter relative to \(G\): whenever \(p_n\in G\) and \(p_n\to p\in G\), one has \(x(p_n)\to x(p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generic stability means that uniquely selected minimizers vary continuously on a residual set of perturbation parameters.
knowledge_statements.title: Generic Stability

children.title: Instability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Exceptional regimes exhibiting nonuniqueness or unstable minimizers.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimizer is unique for \(p\le0\), while \(\operatorname*{argmin}f_p=\{-\sqrt{p/2},\sqrt{p/2}\}\) for \(p>0\); hence \(p=0\) is a boundary of uniqueness stability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bifurcation example marking loss of uniqueness under arbitrarily small perturbations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Characterizations of Well-Posedness and Sensitivity Analysis p. 377
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R\), consider \(f_p(x)=x^4-px^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). If \(p\le0\), then \(x=0\) is the unique global minimizer. If \(p>0\), then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}f_p(x)=\left\{-\sqrt{p/2},\sqrt{p/2}\right\}.\] Consequently, every neighborhood of \(p=0\) contains parameters with a unique minimizer and parameters with two minimizers. The parameter \(p=0\) is therefore an instability boundary for uniqueness and single-valued solution selection, despite continuous dependence of the minimizing set in a weaker set-valued sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quartic family changes from one minimizer to two across zero, making zero a sharp boundary for uniqueness-based stability.
knowledge_statements.title: Instability Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(0,1)\) have the Euclidean metric, and define \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(x)=x\). For \(\varepsilon=1/2\), \(\lambda=1\), and \(x_0=1/4\), one has \(f(x_0)\le\inf_X f+\varepsilon\). Nevertheless, there is no \(\bar x\in X\) such that \[f(\bar x)<f(x)+\frac{\varepsilon}{\lambda}|x-\bar x|\qquad\text{for every }x\in X\setminus\{\bar x\}.\] Hence the complete-space perturbed-minimality conclusion can fail on an incomplete metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the incomplete open interval, the displayed approximate minimizer does not yield an Ekeland-type strict perturbed minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(C=(0,1)\), and define \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(x)=x\). Then \[\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=0,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)=\varnothing.\] For the closed enlargement \(\overline C=[0,1]\), one has \[0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\overline C}f(x).\] Thus nonclosedness causes attainment failure in the original model, while passage to the closure restores attainment by enlarging the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous objective does not attain its infimum on the nonclosed feasible interval, while its closed enlargement admits a minimizer.

\(\operatorname{cl}g\) is the greatest lower-semicontinuous function majorized by \(g\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Closure repair replaces \(g\) by its lower-semicontinuous envelope \(\operatorname{cl}g\), characterized by \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}g)=\overline{\operatorname{epi}g}\) whenever the epigraph closure is itself an epigraph. One always has \(\operatorname{cl}g\le g\), hence \(\inf_X\operatorname{cl}g\le\inf_X g\). The interface is value-exact when equality holds; a repaired minimizer \(\bar x\) solves the original problem whenever additionally \(g(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epigraphical closure produces a lower-semicontinuous model; value equality and equality at a repaired minimizer determine whether the repair transfers back.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequential relaxation of \(f\) is represented by \[\bar f(x)=\inf\left\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(x_n):x_n\to x\right\}.\] It is lower semicontinuous and satisfies \(\bar f\le f\). There is no relaxation gap precisely when \(\inf_X\bar f=\inf_X f\). A relaxed minimizer \(\bar x\) is approximable without value loss when a recovery sequence \(x_n\to\bar x\) exists with \(f(x_n)\to\bar f(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation takes the best limiting cost along convergent sequences. Exactness means equal infima, while recovery sequences approximate relaxed minimizers without value loss.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-order optimality for a differentiable–convex composite problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the generally necessary local condition from its necessary-and-sufficient convex specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper and let \(g:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper and convex, with \(\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). For \((P):\min_{x\in\mathbb{E}} f(x)+g(x)\): (a) if \(x^*\in\operatorname{dom}g\) is a local minimizer and \(f\) is differentiable at \(x^*\), then \(-\nabla f(x^*)\in\partial g(x^*)\); (b) if, in addition, \(f\) is convex and differentiable at \(x^*\in\operatorname{dom}g\), then \(x^*\) is a global minimizer of \((P)\) if and only if \(-\nabla f(x^*)\in\partial g(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer of a differentiable-plus-convex composite objective satisfies composite stationarity. If the differentiable term is also convex, that condition is equivalent to global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local minimizer}\Rightarrow-\nabla f(x^*)\in\partial g(x^*);\qquad f\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\bigl[x^*\text{ global minimizer}\Longleftrightarrow-\nabla f(x^*)\in\partial g(x^*)\bigr]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-quadratic Hilbert-space optimality condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient first-order condition for convex quadratic tracking over a convex admissible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U,H\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(\varnothing\ne U_{ad}\subset U\) be convex, let \(y_d\in H\), let \(\lambda\ge0\), and let \(S:U\to H\) be continuous and linear. Then \(\bar u\in U_{ad}\) minimizes \(J(u)=\tfrac12\|Su-y_d\|_H^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|u\|_U^2\) over \(U_{ad}\) if and only if \(\bigl(S^*(S\bar u-y_d)+\lambda\bar u,u-\bar u\bigr)_U\ge0\) for every \(u\in U_{ad}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A control solves the convex linear-quadratic tracking problem exactly when its gradient satisfies the admissible-set variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: S:U\to H\text{ is continuous and linear}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar u\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in U_{ad}}\left(\tfrac12\|Su-y_d\|_H^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|u\|_U^2\right)\iff\bigl(S^*(S\bar u-y_d)+\lambda\bar u,u-\bar u\bigr)_U\ge0\quad\forall u\in U_{ad}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Conditions for Pointwise Box Constraints in L2
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity and pointwise complementarity for an optimal control subject to almost-everywhere lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $U=L^2(\Omega)$, where $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is bounded and open, and let $\underline u,\bar u\in U$ satisfy $\underline u\le\bar u$ almost everywhere. Define $U_{ad}=\{u\in U:\underline u\le u\le\bar u\ \text{a.e.}\}$ and $L(u,\lambda,\mu)=f(u)+\langle\lambda,\underline u-u\rangle_U+\langle\mu,u-\bar u\rangle_U$. If $f$ is differentiable and $\widehat u$ minimizes $f$ over $U_{ad}$, then there exist $\lambda,\mu\in U$ with $\lambda,\mu\ge0$ almost everywhere such that $\nabla f(\widehat u)-\lambda+\mu=0$ and $\lambda(\widehat u-\underline u)=\mu(\bar u-\widehat u)=0$ almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal pointwise box-constrained control in L2 admits nonnegative lower- and upper-bound multipliers satisfying stationarity and almost-everywhere complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda,\mu\in U:\ \lambda,\mu\ge0\ \text{a.e.},\quad \nabla f(\widehat u)-\lambda+\mu=0,\quad \lambda(\widehat u-\underline u)=0,\quad \mu(\bar u-\widehat u)=0\ \text{a.e.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local and Global Minimum Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained minimization of a function on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a point \(x^*\) is a local minimum point if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(f(x)\ge f(x^*)\) whenever \(\|x-x^*\|\le\varepsilon\). It is a global minimum point if \(f(x)\ge f(x^*)\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary and sufficient KKT conditions for convex inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth convex multiplier characterization under the stated domain-interiority and strict-feasibility qualification, including Lagrangian minimality and the Gâteaux-differentiable specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\), let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with \(m\ge1\), and let \(g_i\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\) for every \(i\in I\). Assume
\[
(\forall i\in I)\quad \operatorname{lev}_{\leq0}g_i\subset\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom}g_i,
\qquad
\operatorname{dom}f\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}\operatorname{lev}_{<0}g_i\neq\varnothing.
\]
Then \(\bar x\in\mathcal H\) solves
\[
\min\{f(x):g_i(x)\leq0\ (i\in I)\}
\]
if and only if there exist \((\bar\nu_i)_{i\in I}\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(u_i\in\partial g_i(\bar x)\) such that
\[
-\sum_{i\in I}\bar\nu_i u_i\in\partial f(\bar x),
\qquad
(\forall i\in I)\quad g_i(\bar x)\leq0,
\quad \bar\nu_i g_i(\bar x)=0.
\]
For such multipliers, \(\bar x\) minimizes \(f+\sum_{i\in I}\bar\nu_i g_i\) over \(\mathcal H\). If \(f\) and every \(g_i\) are G\^ateaux differentiable at \(\bar x\), stationarity becomes
\[
\nabla f(\bar x)=-\sum_{i\in I}\bar\nu_i\nabla g_i(\bar x),
\]
with the same multiplier nonnegativity, feasibility, and complementary-slackness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex objective and finitely many proper lower-semicontinuous convex inequality functions satisfying the stated domain-interiority and strict-feasibility conditions, a point is optimal exactly when nonnegative multipliers and constraint subgradients satisfy stationarity, primal feasibility, and complementary slackness. It then minimizes the associated unconstrained Lagrangian. Under Gâteaux differentiability, subgradient stationarity reduces to the gradient KKT equation.

assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is a local minimizer and every ray \(\bar x+tv\) is locally admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_D^-(\bar x;v)\ge0\) for every \(v\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower one-sided Dini stationarity for unconstrained local minima.

source_refs.locator: 8.2 Dini Stationarity p. 736
source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the lower Dini directional derivative by \[f_D^-(\bar x;v)=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{f(\bar x+tv)-f(\bar x)}{t}.\] Because \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer, the numerator is nonnegative for all sufficiently small \(t>0\). Hence \(f_D^-(\bar x;v)\ge0\) for every \(v\in X\). This necessary condition uses fixed directions and does not impose stability under perturbations of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an unconstrained local minimum, every lower one-sided Dini directional derivative is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Dini Directional Stationarity

source_witnesses.locator: 8.2 Dini Stationarity p. 736
source_witnesses.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-Dini necessary condition is mathematically valid in the asserted normed-space setting, but the cited source is explicitly finite-dimensional and therefore does not support that scope. The statement also includes proof text. A source covering the normed-space version is required.

children.title: Hadamard Directional Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Directionally stable perturbation regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space and \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\).
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is a local minimizer with a neighborhood contained in the effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_H^-(\bar x;v)\ge0\) for every \(v\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower Hadamard stationarity, stable under perturbation of directions.

source_refs.locator: 4.1.1 Generalized directional derivatives p. 159

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The lower Hadamard directional derivative is \[f_H^-(\bar x;v)=\liminf_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\w\to v}}\frac{f(\bar x+tw)-f(\bar x)}{t}.\] At a local minimizer \(\bar x\), one has \(f_H^-(\bar x;v)\ge0\) for every \(v\in X\). Unlike the fixed-direction Dini derivative, this stationarity condition tests directions \(w\) converging to \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer has nonnegative lower Hadamard derivatives in every direction, including along nearby directions converging to the tested direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Hadamard Directional Stationarity

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1.1 Generalized directional derivatives p. 159

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SDP value derivative under unique multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order value sensitivity when every primal optimum has a unique multiplier matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the inf-compactness condition holds and, for every \(x\in\mathcal S(P)\), the Lagrange-multiplier set is the singleton \(\Lambda(x)=\{\bar\Omega(x)\}\). Then the optimal-value function \(v\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(u_0\), and for every direction \(d\),
\[
v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(P)}d\cdot\nabla_uL\bigl(x,\bar\Omega(x),u_0\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the SDP is inf-compact and each primal optimal solution has a unique Lagrange multiplier matrix, then the value function is Hadamard directionally differentiable. Its directional derivative is the infimum over primal optima of the parameter derivative of the Lagrangian evaluated at the corresponding unique multiplier.
assumptions_latex: d\text{ is an admissible parameter direction}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is Hadamard directionally differentiable at }u_0,\qquad v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(P)}d\cdot\nabla_uL\bigl(x,\bar\Omega(x),u_0\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional derivative of a convex SDP value function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order perturbation formula using primal and dual solution sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the unperturbed semidefinite program \((P)\) is convex and satisfies the Slater and inf-compactness conditions. Then its optimal-value function \(v\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(u_0\), and for every \(d\in U\),
\[
v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(P)}\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal S(D)} d\cdot\nabla_uL(x,\Omega,u_0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex SDP satisfying Slater regularity and inf-compactness, the value function is Hadamard directionally differentiable at the reference parameter. In every direction, its derivative is the infimum over primal optimal solutions of the supremum, over dual optimal solutions, of the parameter derivative of the Lagrangian.
assumptions_latex: \((P)\) is a convex semidefinite program at \(u_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\text{ is Hadamard directionally differentiable at }u_0,\qquad v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(P)}\sup_{\Omega\in\mathcal S(D)}d\cdot\nabla_uL(x,\Omega,u_0).

children.title: Bouligand Directional Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Contingent directional regimes for nonsmooth models.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space, \(C\subset X\), and \(\bar x\in C\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\).
\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(\bar x;v)\ge0\) for every \(v\in T_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained Bouligand stationarity on the contingent tangent cone under directionally stable differentiability.

source_refs.locator: 4.1.1 Generalized directional derivatives p. 159

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Bouligand contingent tangent cone is \[T_C(\bar x)=\left\{v\in X:\exists\,t_n\downarrow0,\ v_n\to v,\ \bar x+t_nv_n\in C\right\}.\] If \(f\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at the constrained local minimizer \(\bar x\), then Bouligand stationarity holds: \[f'(\bar x;v)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }v\in T_C(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a constrained local minimum, a Hadamard directionally differentiable objective has a nonnegative directional derivative along every direction in the Bouligand contingent tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Bouligand Directional Stationarity

children.title: Clarke Directional Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Convexified generalized-directional regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally closed near \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{\circ}(\bar x;d)\ge 0\quad\text{for every }d\in T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized directional derivative of f at x in direction d
Clarke tangent cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained Clarke directional stationarity for a locally Lipschitz objective in finite dimensions.

source_refs.locator: F. Tangent-Normal Relations p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible point \(\bar x\) is Clarke directionally stationary for minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) when the Clarke generalized directional derivative is nonnegative along every Clarke-tangent direction:
\[
f^{\circ}(\bar x;d)\ge 0\qquad\text{for all }d\in T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x).
\]
This condition uses the robust, convexified tangent geometry and the upper generalized directional derivative; it does not assert nonnegativity of every more selective nonconvex directional derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clarke directional stationarity means that the Clarke generalized directional derivative is nonnegative in every Clarke-tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Directional Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equilibrium-feasible tangent directions satisfy a multiplier-dependent AVI
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary tangent-direction characterization under SBCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\bar z\in\mathcal F\), let \(d_z=(d_x,d_y)\in T(\bar z;\mathcal F)\), and suppose that SBCQ holds at \(\bar z\). Then \(d_z\in T(\bar z;Z)\), and there exists \(\lambda\in M(\bar z)\) such that
\[d_y\in\operatorname{SOL}\!\left(\nabla_xL(\bar z,\lambda)d_x,\nabla_yL(\bar z,\lambda),\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;d_x)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under SBCQ, every tangent direction to the equilibrium-feasible region is tangent to the explicit constraint set, and its lower-level component solves the corresponding multiplier-dependent affine variational inequality for some reference-point multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_z\in T(\bar z;Z)\quad\text{and}\quad\exists\lambda\in M(\bar z):\ d_y\in\operatorname{SOL}\!\left(\nabla_xL(\bar z,\lambda)d_x,\nabla_yL(\bar z,\lambda),\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;d_x)\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Critical-cone representations under multiplier existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation theorem, with the multiplier-orthogonality formula conditional on the absence of the set constraint \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0\in\Phi\) be feasible and suppose \(\Lambda(x_0)\neq\varnothing\). Then \(h=0\) is an optimal solution of the linearized problem and
\[
C(x_0)=\{h\in T_Q(x_0):DG(x_0)h\in T_K(G(x_0)),\ Df(x_0)h=0\}.
\]
If, in addition, \(Q=X\), then for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0)\),
\[
C(x_0)=\{h\in X:DG(x_0)h\in T_K(G(x_0)),\ \langle\lambda,DG(x_0)h\rangle=0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point with a Lagrange multiplier, zero solves the linearized problem and the critical cone consists of linearized feasible directions with zero objective derivative. When Q equals the whole space, every multiplier yields the stated orthogonality representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\operatorname*{argmin}(3.15),\quad C(x_0)=\{h\in T_Q(x_0):DG(x_0)h\in T_K(G(x_0)),\ Df(x_0)h=0\};\quad Q=X\Rightarrow (\forall\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0))\ C(x_0)=\{h\in X:DG(x_0)h\in T_K(G(x_0)),\ \langle\lambda,DG(x_0)h\rangle=0\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-order necessary condition on the linearization cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified specialization of tangent-cone first-order optimality for Banach-space conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W,V\) be Banach spaces, let \(J:W\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:W\to V\) be continuously Fréchet differentiable, let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subset W\) be closed and convex, and let \(\mathcal K_G\subset V\) be a closed convex cone. If \(\bar w\) is a local solution over \(F_{\mathrm{ad}}\) and
\[
L(F_{\mathrm{ad}},G,\mathcal K_G,\mathcal C;\bar w)\subset T(F_{\mathrm{ad}};\bar w),
\]
then
\[
\bar w\in F_{\mathrm{ad}},\qquad \langle J'(\bar w),s\rangle_{W^*,W}\ge0\quad\forall s\in L(F_{\mathrm{ad}},G,\mathcal K_G,\mathcal C;\bar w).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the tangent–linearization qualification, the derivative at a local solution is nonnegative along every linearized feasible direction.
assumptions_latex: J:W\to\mathbb R\text{ and }G:W\to V\text{ are continuously Fréchet differentiable}
\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subset W\text{ is closed and convex}
\mathcal K_G\subset V\text{ is a closed convex cone}
\bar w\text{ is a local solution over }F_{\mathrm{ad}}
L(F_{\mathrm{ad}},G,\mathcal K_G,\mathcal C;\bar w)\subset T(F_{\mathrm{ad}};\bar w)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar w\in F_{\mathrm{ad}}\ \text{and}\ \langle J'(\bar w),s\rangle_{W^*,W}\ge0\quad\forall s\in L(F_{\mathrm{ad}},G,\mathcal K_G,\mathcal C;\bar w)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential tangent cone

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varnothing\ne F_{\mathrm{ad}}\subset W\) and \(w\in F_{\mathrm{ad}}\). Then

T(F_{\mathrm{ad}};w)=\left\{s\in W:\exists\,\eta_k>0,\ w_k\in F_{\mathrm{ad}},\ w_k\to w,\ \eta_k(w_k-w)\to s\right\}.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar cone formula for a linear preimage–cone intersection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Banach-space convex-cone calculus; the equality requires the stated surjectivity-type condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be Banach spaces, let \(A:X\to Y\) be continuous and linear, and let \(C\subset X\) and \(K\subset Y\) be closed convex cones. Then
\[
A^*(K^-)+C^-\subseteq \bigl(A^{-1}(K)\cap C\bigr)^-.
\]
If additionally \(A(C)-K=Y\), then
\[
A^*(K^-)+C^-=\bigl(A^{-1}(K)\cap C\bigr)^-.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed convex cones C and K in Banach spaces and a continuous linear map A, the sum of the adjoint image of the negative polar of K and the negative polar of C is contained in the negative polar of the intersection of C with the inverse image of K. Equality holds when A(C)−K equals the whole codomain.
assumptions_latex: A:X\to Y\text{ is continuous and linear}
C\subset X\text{ and }K\subset Y\text{ are closed convex cones}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^*(K^-)+C^-\subseteq\bigl(A^{-1}(K)\cap C\bigr)^-,\quad A(C)-K=Y\implies A^*(K^-)+C^-=\bigl(A^{-1}(K)\cap C\bigr)^-

knowledge_statements.statement_title: AVI solution maps and the equilibrium-feasible linearized cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-indexed linearization of a parameterized VI solution-graph constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(\lambda\in M(\bar z)\), define
\[\mathcal{LS}_{(\bar z,\lambda)}(d_x)=\operatorname{SOL}\!\left(\nabla_xL(\bar z,\lambda)d_x,\nabla_yL(\bar z,\lambda),\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;d_x)\right).\]
Define
\[\mathcal L(\bar z;\mathcal F)=T(\bar z;Z)\cap\left(\bigcup_{\lambda\in M(\bar z)}\operatorname{Gr}\mathcal{LS}_{(\bar z,\lambda)}\right).\]
Under SBCQ,
\[T(\bar z;\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal L(\bar z;\mathcal F).\]
The set \(\mathcal L(\bar z;\mathcal F)\) is a closed cone that may be nonconvex. For each fixed \(\lambda\), \(\operatorname{Gr}\mathcal{LS}_{(\bar z,\lambda)}\) is a finite union of polyhedral cones. If the multiplier is unique, the union over multipliers reduces to the graph associated with that multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each multiplier, the linearized solution map assigns to a parameter direction the solutions of an affine VI. The intersection of the union of these graphs with the tangent cone to the explicit constraints is a closed, possibly nonconvex linearized cone containing the true feasible tangent cone under SBCQ. Each fixed-multiplier graph is a finite union of polyhedral cones, and multiplier uniqueness eliminates the graph union.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K(\bar z,\lambda;d_x)\text{ is polyhedral and the AVI data are affine for the fixed-multiplier graph structure}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(\bar z;\mathcal F)\subseteq\mathcal L(\bar z;\mathcal F),\qquad\mathcal L(\bar z;\mathcal F)\text{ is a possibly nonconvex closed cone},\qquad\operatorname{Gr}\mathcal{LS}_{(\bar z,\lambda)}\text{ is a finite union of polyhedral cones}

children.title: Feasible-Direction Conditions
children.top_down_role: Minimality on directly realizable directions.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), which is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).

notation.meaning: Cone of directions whose short line segments from x remain feasible

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessity along directly realizable straight-line directions.

source_refs.locator: F. Tangent-Normal Relations p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the feasible-direction cone by
\[
F_C(\bar x):=\left\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:\text{there exists }\varepsilon>0\text{ such that }\bar x+td\in C\text{ for every }t\in[0,\varepsilon]\right\}.
\]
Local minimality and differentiability imply
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\ge 0\qquad\text{for every }d\in F_C(\bar x).
\]
Thus no directly realizable direction is a strict first-order descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a differentiable local minimum, the gradient has nonnegative pairing with every direction whose sufficiently short forward segment remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Conditions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent optimality conditions for constrained convex minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence among global minimality, feasible-direction inequalities, tangent-cone inequalities, and a subgradient-normal inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex, and let \(\bar x\in C\). Then the following are equivalent: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\); \(f'(\bar x;y-\bar x)\ge 0\) for every \(y\in C\); \(f'(\bar x;d)\ge 0\) for every \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\); and \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex minimization over a closed convex set, a feasible point is optimal exactly when every feasible or tangent direction has nonnegative directional derivative, equivalently when zero belongs to the sum of the subdifferential and normal cone.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The direction family \(\Upsilon_\eta(x_0)\) and the named first-order growth condition are retained because their definitions are not included in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\) be feasible for \((P)\). (i) If there exist \(\alpha>0\) and \(\eta>0\) such that \(Df(x_0)h\geq\alpha\|h\|\) for every \(h\in\Upsilon_\eta(x_0)\), then the first-order growth condition holds at \(x_0\). (ii) If \(DG(x_0)(T_Q(x_0))-T_K(G(x_0))=Y\) and the same inequality holds for some \(\alpha>0\) with \(\eta=0\), then the first-order growth condition holds at \(x_0\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, uniform positive derivative growth on Upsilon_eta with positive eta is sufficient for first-order growth. Under the stated tangent-cone regularity, eta may be zero. Under Robinson's constraint qualification, the corresponding inequality on Upsilon_0 is equivalent to first-order growth.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), which is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand or contingent tangent cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The contingent tangent cone is
\[
T_C(\bar x):=\left\{d:\text{there exist }t_k\downarrow0\text{ and }x_k\in C\text{ with }x_k\to\bar x\text{ and }(x_k-\bar x)/t_k\to d\right\}.
\]
If \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) on \(C\), then
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for all }d\in T_C(\bar x).
\]
Equivalently, the negative gradient belongs to the polar of the contingent tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a smooth constrained local minimum, the gradient pairs nonnegatively with every Bouligand contingent-tangent direction.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(d\) belongs to \(T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)\) when, for every sequence \(x_k\to\bar x\) with \(x_k\in C\) and every \(t_k\downarrow0\), there exist \(d_k\to d\) such that \(x_k+t_kd_k\in C\). Local minimality implies
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for every }d\in T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x).
\]
The cone is closed and convex, so this is a convexified robust first-order condition.

children.top_down_role: Minimality on constraint-generated tangent approximations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I(\bar x):=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\) and define
\[
L_C(\bar x):=\{d:\langle\nabla g_i(\bar x),d\rangle\le0\text{ for }i\in I(\bar x),\ \langle\nabla h_j(\bar x),d\rangle=0\text{ for all }j\}.
\]
The tangent condition and Abadie's equality yield
\[
\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for every }d\in L_C(\bar x).
\]
Without a condition ensuring \(L_C(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x)\), local minimality alone need not imply this stronger linearized-cone inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Abadie's condition, a smooth local minimum has nonnegative gradient pairing with every direction satisfying the linearized active constraints.

children.title: Convex-Normal Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Stationarity for convex feasible geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C^{\mathrm{cvx}}(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Convex-analysis normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth-objective stationarity over a convex feasible set.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The convex normal cone is
\[
N_C^{\mathrm{cvx}}(\bar x):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le0\text{ for every }x\in C\}.
\]
Convex-normal stationarity is the inclusion
\[
-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C^{\mathrm{cvx}}(\bar x),
\]
equivalently \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),x-\bar x\rangle\ge0\) for every \(x\in C\). Every local minimizer of the differentiable objective over the convex set satisfies this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex-normal stationarity places the negative gradient in the convex normal cone, equivalently giving a variational inequality over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Normal Stationarity

children.title: Regular-Normal Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Stationarity using regular normal geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally closed near \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-\nabla f(\bar x)\in\widehat N_C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Fréchet or regular normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fréchet-normal stationarity for a smooth objective on a locally closed set.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Regular-normal stationarity is
\[
-\nabla f(\bar x)\in\widehat N_C(\bar x),
\]
where
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x):=\left\{v:\limsup_{\substack{x\to\bar x,\ x\in C\\x\ne\bar x}}\frac{\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle}{\|x-\bar x\|}\le0\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(\langle\nabla f(\bar x),d\rangle\ge0\) for every \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\). A differentiable local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\) satisfies this inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular-normal stationarity places the negative gradient in the Fréchet normal cone; every smooth constrained local minimum satisfies it.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The limiting normal cone is the outer limit
\[
N_C(\bar x):=\left\{v:\text{there exist }x_k\to\bar x,\ x_k\in C,\ v_k\to v,\ v_k\in\widehat N_C(x_k)\right\}.
\]
Limiting-normal stationarity is
\[
-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C(\bar x).
\]
Because \(\widehat N_C(\bar x)\subset N_C(\bar x)\), every differentiable local minimizer satisfies this inclusion, although the converse generally fails and the limiting cone can be nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limiting-normal stationarity requires the negative gradient to be a limit of nearby regular normals, accommodating nonconvex feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Clarke normal cone is the negative polar
\[
N_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x):=\bigl(T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)\bigr)^{\circ}=\{v:\langle v,d\rangle\le0\text{ for every }d\in T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)\}.
\]
Clarke-normal stationarity is
\[
-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x).
\]
In finite dimensions this cone equals the closed convex hull of \(N_C(\bar x)\). Hence limiting-normal stationarity implies Clarke-normal stationarity, while the reverse implication can fail.

children.title: Indicator-Function Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Extended-real representation of constrained minimality.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally closed near \(\bar x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)\iff-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Indicator function of C, zero on C and positive infinity outside C

source_refs.locator: 2.5.2 Specific Normal and Subdifferential Structures p. 235

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. Then minimizing \(f\) over \(C\) is equivalent to unconstrained minimization of the extended-real function \(f+\delta_C\). The smooth sum rule and the indicator-normal identity give
\[
\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)=\nabla f(\bar x)+N_C(\bar x).
\]
Consequently,
\[
0\in\partial(f+\delta_C)(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad-\nabla f(\bar x)\in N_C(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the feasible-set indicator converts constrained stationarity into unconstrained limiting-subdifferential stationarity and reproduces limiting-normal stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Function Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Subdifferential stationarity for \(\varphi\) at \(\bar x\) is the inclusion
\[
0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x).
\]
If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer, then directly from the regular-subgradient inequality,
\[
0\in\widehat\partial\varphi(\bar x).
\]
Since \(\widehat\partial\varphi(\bar x)\subset\partial\varphi(\bar x)\), every local minimizer is limiting-subdifferentially stationary. This is a necessary condition only; without additional structure, a stationary point need not be locally minimizing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-dimensional local minimizer has zero as a regular, and therefore limiting, subgradient; this stationarity condition is not sufficient in general.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal–Subdifferential Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact indicator-function correspondence for regular and limiting constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the indicator function \(\delta_C\), regular subgradients are exactly regular normals and limiting subgradients are exactly limiting normals:
\[
\widehat\partial\delta_C(\bar x)=\widehat N_C(\bar x),
\qquad
\partial\delta_C(\bar x)=N_C(\bar x).
\]
Thus normal-cone constructions for sets are represented by the corresponding subdifferential constructions for indicator functions, with the regular or limiting type preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regular and limiting subdifferentials of a set indicator equal, respectively, the regular and limiting normal cones to that set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable finite-dimensional convex formulation on a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in C\), convexity gives the first-order inequality \[f(x)\geq f(x^*)+\langle\nabla f(x^*),x-x^*\rangle.\] Consequently, if \(x^*\) satisfies the variational inequality \[\langle\nabla f(x^*),x-x^*\rangle\geq0\qquad\text{for all }x\in C,\] then \(f(x)\geq f(x^*)\) for every \(x\in C\), and hence \(x^*\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Principle and Weak Minimum-Principle Sufficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two solution-set sufficiency properties for a variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A variational inequality (K,F) satisfies minimum-principle sufficiency (MPS) if there exists x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F) such that
\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{x\in K:F(x^*)^T(x^*-x)=0\}.
It satisfies weak minimum-principle sufficiency (WMPS) if there exists x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F) such that
\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{x\in K:F(x)^T(x^*-x)\ge0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MPS means that, for some solution, the full VI solution set is exactly the set on which its fixed operator value gives zero pairing with the displacement. WMPS instead characterizes the solution set using the operator value at each candidate and a nonnegative pairing with the displacement from that candidate to the fixed solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{MPS}:\ \operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{x\in K:F(x^*)^T(x^*-x)=0\};\qquad \mathrm{WMPS}:\ \operatorname{SOL}(K,F)=\{x\in K:F(x)^T(x^*-x)\ge0\}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^3\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Then \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \[f'(0)=0,\] so \(0\) is stationary. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive definiteness induced by a sufficiently large quadratic equality penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-penalty stabilization for full-row-rank linear equality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and let \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m\). If \(x^TAx>0\) for every nonzero \(x\in\ker C\), then there exist \(K_0>0\) and \(\alpha>0\) such that \[A+KC^TC\succeq \alpha I\qquad\text{for every }K\ge K_0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a symmetric quadratic form is positive definite on the nullspace of a full-row-rank equality matrix, adding a sufficiently large quadratic equality penalty makes it uniformly positive definite on the whole space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K_0>0,\ \exists\alpha>0,\ \forall K\ge K_0:\ A+KC^TC\succeq\alpha I

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegative linear functional on a nullspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear equality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(L=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=0\}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). If \(\langle c,x\rangle\ge 0\) for every \(x\in L\), then there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(c=A^Ty\), and \(\langle c,x\rangle=0\) for every \(x\in L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a linear functional is nonnegative on the entire nullspace of a matrix, then it vanishes there and its coefficient vector lies in the range of the transposed matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y\in\mathbb R^m:\ c=A^Ty\quad\text{and}\quad\forall x\in L,\ \langle c,x\rangle=0

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inequality constraints impose componentwise nonpositivity. At a feasible point, active constraints are exactly those holding with equality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Generalized-Gradient Bound on an Arc Tube
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting boundedness result for the nonsmooth variational multiplier construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be the piecewise-smooth arc in the preceding problem, so that \(\{(x(t),\dot x(t)):t\in[0,1]\}\) and its unit tube are bounded. If \(\phi\) is Lipschitz on bounded sets, then there exists \(M<\infty\) such that, for every \(t\in[0,1]\), every \((s,v)\in(x(t),\dot x(t))+B\), and every \(\zeta\in\partial\phi(s,v)\), one has \(|\zeta|\le M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The generalized gradients of a function that is Lipschitz on bounded sets are uniformly bounded throughout the unit tube around the arc and its velocity.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is the piecewise-smooth arc from the preceding problem and its unit phase-space tube is bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists M<\infty\ \forall t,s,v,\zeta:\ |\zeta|\le M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite max-function and loss of smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a finite pointwise maximum and records that smooth component functions do not ensure differentiability of the maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given functions $g_i:C\to\mathbf R$ for $i=0,\ldots,m$, their finite max-function is $g(x)=\max_{0\le i\le m}g_i(x)$. Even when every $g_i$ is smooth, $g$ need not be differentiable, so an ordinary gradient of $g$ need not exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite max-function is the pointwise maximum of finitely many component functions. It may be nonsmooth even when all components are smooth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(x)=\max_{0\le i\le m}g_i(x),\qquad (\forall i,\ g_i\text{ smooth})\not\Rightarrow g\text{ differentiable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Arc Optimality for the Auxiliary Differential Inclusion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local reduction from the original path-constrained problem to the constructed differential-inclusion problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\), \(\varepsilon_K\), and \(F_K\) be as in the preceding construction. The arc \(z(t)\equiv0\) minimizes \(f(x(1)+z(1))\) over all arcs \(z\) satisfying \(|z(t)|<\varepsilon_K/(2N)\), \(z(0)\in C_0-x(0)\), \(z(1)\in C_1-x(1)\), and \(\dot z(t)\in F_K(t,z(t))\) a.e. Every such admissible arc satisfies \(\phi(x(t)+z(t),\dot x(t)+\dot z(t))\le0\) a.e.; consequently, the optimality of \(x\) for the original problem gives \(f(x(1))\le f(x(1)+z(1))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every sufficiently small arc admitted by the constructed differential inclusion preserves the original path constraint, so the zero perturbation minimizes the auxiliary problem.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is optimal for the original variational problem}
N,\varepsilon_K,F_K\text{ are defined by the preceding construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi(x+z,\dot x+\dot z)\le0\text{ a.e. and }f(x(1))\le f(x(1)+z(1));\text{ hence }z\equiv0\text{ minimizes the auxiliary problem.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Point of a Conic Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gateaux-differentiable vector inequalities in an ordered normed space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a vector space, let \(Z\) be a normed space ordered by a positive cone \(P\) with \(\operatorname{int}P\neq\varnothing\), and let \(G:X\to Z\) have a Gateaux differential linear in its increment. A point \(x_0\in X\) is regular for \(G(x)\leq\theta\) if \(G(x_0)\leq\theta\) and there exists \(h\in X\) such that \(G(x_0)+\delta G(x_0;h)<\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is regular for the conic inequality when some direction makes its linearized constraint strictly feasible.
assumptions_latex: Z\text{ is a normed space ordered by a positive cone }P
G:X\to Z\text{ is Gateaux differentiable and }\delta G(x;\cdot)\text{ is linear}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0\text{ is regular}\iff \exists h\in X:\ G(x_0)+\delta G(x_0;h)<\theta
