knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hidden-Convexity Separation under Endpoint Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a convex-hull exclusion condition for optimal finite-difference solutions with essential and inessential endpoint inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \{(\bar u_N(\cdot),\bar x_N(\cdot))\} be optimal solutions of (P_N), and suppose \varphi_i=0 for i=m+1,\ldots,m+r. In addition to the standing assumptions, suppose that \varphi_i is continuously differentiable around the limiting point or points of \{\bar x_N(b)\} for i=0,\ldots,m, that \{\bar u_N(\cdot)\} is proper, and that the first l\in\{1,\ldots,m\} inequality constraints are essential while the remaining inequalities are inessential. Then there exists a sequence e_N\in\mathbb R^{l+1} with e_N=o(h_N) as h_N\to0 such that (\operatorname{co}S_N+e_N)\cap\mathbb R_{<}^{l+1}=\varnothing for all sufficiently large N.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standing assumptions, endpoint smoothness, properness of the reference controls, and the stated essential–inessential classification, the convex hull of the discrete primal variation set, after an error smaller than the mesh size, does not intersect the strictly negative orthant for all sufficiently large discretizations.
assumptions_latex: \text{the standing assumptions of the discrete approximation problems hold}
\varphi_i\in C^1\text{ around the limiting endpoint point or points}\quad(i=0,\ldots,m)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists e_N\in\mathbb R^{l+1},\ e_N=o(h_N):\quad (\operatorname{co}S_N+e_N)\cap\mathbb R_{<}^{l+1}=\varnothing\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }N.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Rule for Multiple Variational Path Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-constraint multiplier rule under a generalized-gradient rank condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the piecewise-smooth arc \(x\) minimize \(f(y(1))\) over arcs \(y\) satisfying \(y(0)\in C_0\), \(y(1)\in C_1\), and \(\phi_i(y,\dot y)\le0\) a.e. for \(i=1,\ldots,r\), where \(f,\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_r\) are locally Lipschitz. Suppose that, for every \(t\), every \((\zeta_1,\zeta_2)\in\operatorname{co}\!\left(\bigcup_{i:\,\phi_i(x(t),\dot x(t))=0}\partial\phi_i(x(t),\dot x(t))\right)\) satisfies \(\zeta_2\ne0\). Then there exist an arc \(p\), measurable functions \(\lambda_i\), and \(\lambda_0\in\{0,1\}\) such that \(\binom{\dot p(t)}{p(t)}\in\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i(t)\partial\phi_i(x(t),\dot x(t))\) a.e.; \(\lambda_i(t)\ge0\) a.e. and \(\lambda_i(t)=0\) whenever \(\phi_i(x(t),\dot x(t))<0\); \(p(0)\in N_{C_0}(x(0))\); \(-p(1)\in\lambda_0\partial f(x(1))+N_{C_1}(x(1))\); and \(|p(t)|+\lambda_0\ne0\) for every \(t\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated active-generalized-gradient rank condition, finitely many locally Lipschitz path inequalities admit nonnegative complementary multipliers, an adjoint inclusion, endpoint transversality, and nontriviality.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ minimizes the stated endpoint-constrained problem with }\phi_i(y,\dot y)\le0\text{ a.e.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists p,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r,\lambda_0\text{ satisfying the summed adjoint inclusion, complementarity, endpoint transversality, and nontriviality conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Essential and Inessential Endpoint Inequalities in Finite-Difference Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies a feasible endpoint inequality according to the size of its slack relative to the mesh parameter along a subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible sequence \{(u_N,x_N)\} and a subsequence \mathcal M\subset\mathbb N, the constraint \varphi_i(x_N(b))\le\gamma_{iN} is essential along \mathcal M if \varphi_i(x_N(b))-\gamma_{iN}=O(h_N), equivalently if there exists K_i\ge0 such that -K_ih_N\le\varphi_i(x_N(b))-\gamma_{iN}\le0 for N\to\infty,\ N\in\mathcal M. It is inessential along \mathcal M if, for every K>0, there exists N_0 such that \varphi_i(x_N(b))-\gamma_{iN}\le-Kh_N for all N\ge N_0 with N\in\mathcal M. The extract writes the first asymptotic qualification as h_N\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Along a subsequence of feasible discrete solutions, an endpoint inequality is essential when its nonpositive slack remains within a fixed multiple of the mesh size. It is inessential when its slack eventually lies below every negative multiple of the mesh size. The extract's first big-O display explicitly writes h_N tending to infinity, although its equivalent bound is indexed by N tending to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{essential}\iff\exists K_i\ge0:\ -K_ih_N\le\varphi_i(x_N(b))-\gamma_{iN}\le0;\qquad \text{inessential}\iff\forall K>0\ \exists N_0\ \forall N\in\mathcal M,\ N\ge N_0:\ \varphi_i(x_N(b))-\gamma_{iN}\le-Kh_N.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Kuhn–Tucker Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary multiplier conditions for Gateaux-differentiable conic inequality-constrained optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a vector space and \(Z\) a normed space ordered by a positive cone \(P\) with \(\operatorname{int}P\neq\varnothing\). Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:X\to Z\) be Gateaux differentiable, with differentials linear in their increments. If \(x_0\) minimizes \(f\) subject to \(G(x)\leq\theta\) and is regular, meaning that \(G(x_0)+\delta G(x_0;h)<\theta\) for some \(h\in X\), then there exists \(z_0^*\in Z^*\) with \(z_0^*\geq\theta\) such that \(f+\langle G,z_0^*\rangle\) is stationary at \(x_0\) and \(\langle G(x_0),z_0^*\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular minimizer of a differentiable conic inequality problem, a nonnegative continuous linear multiplier exists for which the Lagrangian is stationary and complementary slackness holds.
assumptions_latex: Z\text{ is a normed space ordered by a positive cone }P
f:X\to\mathbb R\text{ and }G:X\to Z\text{ are Gateaux differentiable with increment-linear differentials}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists z_0^*\in Z^*,\ z_0^*\geq\theta:\ \delta f(x_0;v)+\langle\delta G(x_0;v),z_0^*\rangle=0\ \forall v\in X,\quad \langle G(x_0),z_0^*\rangle=0

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order geometry induced by active smooth inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a real Banach space, let \(m\in\mathbb{N}\), and let \(g_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) be Fréchet differentiable at \(\bar x\in C\), where \[C:=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq 0\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Define the active-index set by \(I(\bar x):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). The active-set linearization is \[L_C(\bar x):=\{d\in X:Dg_i(\bar x)d\leq0\ \text{for every }i\in I(\bar x)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many differentiable inequalities, the active-set linearization consists of directions satisfying the linearized inequalities associated with constraints that are tight at the reference feasible point.

For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), \(g_i:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is Fréchet differentiable at the feasible point \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-set constraints represented by indicators and normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometric constraint requires \(x\in\Omega\), where \(X\) is a Banach space and \(\Omega\subset X\) is a prescribed closed set. Define \(\delta_\Omega:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(\delta_\Omega(x)=0\) for \(x\in\Omega\) and \(\delta_\Omega(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. For every proper function \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \[\inf_{x\in\Omega}\varphi(x)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(\varphi(x)+\delta_\Omega(x)\bigr).\] Generalized derivatives of \(\delta_\Omega\) define the corresponding normal cone \(N_\Omega\), with the precise cone determined by the selected generalized-derivative construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in a closed feasible set can be encoded by its indicator function without changing the infimum. The chosen generalized derivative of that indicator determines the corresponding normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space and \(\Omega\subset X\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in\Omega}\varphi(x)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(\varphi(x)+\delta_\Omega(x)\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper-subdifferential condition under a geometric constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary normal-cone inclusions for an extended-real-valued objective at a constrained local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a Banach space, let \(\varphi:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer of \(\varphi\) over \(\Omega\subset X\), with \(\varphi(\bar x)<\infty\). Then
\[
-\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x)\subset\widehat N(\bar x;\Omega)
\quad\text{and}\quad
-\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x)\subset N(\bar x;\Omega).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a constrained local minimum where the objective is finite, every negative regular upper subgradient is both a Fréchet normal and a limiting normal to the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x)\subset\widehat N(\bar x;\Omega)\cap N(\bar x;\Omega)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-order necessary condition under equality operator constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonsmooth multiplier rule for inequality, equality-operator, and set constraints in Asplund spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) be a local solution of \(\min\{\varphi_0(x)\mid \varphi_i(x)\le 0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ f(x)=0,\ x\in\Omega\}\), and set \(I(\bar x):=\{i\mid\varphi_i(\bar x)=0\}\). Suppose \(X\) and \(Y\) are Asplund spaces; \(\varphi_i\) satisfies the scalar-function assumptions of Theorem 5.16; \(\Omega\) is locally closed around \(\bar x\); \(f\) is strictly Lipschitzian at \(\bar x\); and \(f_\Omega^{-1}\) is PSNC at \((f(\bar x),\bar x)\). Then there exist \(\lambda_i\ge 0\) for \(i\in I(\bar x)\cup\{0\}\) and \(y^*\in Y^*\), not all zero, such that \[0\in\partial\!\left(\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)\cup\{0\}}\lambda_i\varphi_i\right)(\bar x)+\partial\langle y^*,f\rangle(\bar x)+N(\bar x;\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated Asplund-space, scalar-function, local-closedness, strict-Lipschitz, and PSNC assumptions, a local minimizer admits nontrivial nonnegative objective and active-inequality multipliers together with an equality multiplier satisfying the generalized stationarity inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) locally solves the stated inequality, equality-operator, and set-constrained problem.
\(\varphi_0\) and the active \(\varphi_i\) are locally Lipschitzian around \(\bar x\), while the inactive \(\varphi_i\) are upper semicontinuous at \(\bar x\).
\(f\) is strictly Lipschitzian at \(\bar x\), and \(f_\Omega^{-1}\) is PSNC at \((f(\bar x),\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\lambda_i\ge0\ (i\in I(\bar x)\cup\{0\}),\ \exists y^*\in Y^*\), not all zero, such that \(0\in\partial(\sum_i\lambda_i\varphi_i)(\bar x)+\partial\langle y^*,f\rangle(\bar x)+N(\bar x;\Omega)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Holonomic constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained variational problems whose constraints can be expressed without derivatives of the dependent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variational constraint is called holonomic when it has, or can be integrated into, the form \(M(x,y(x))=0\), with no dependence on \(y'(x)\). This equation defines a constraint surface in \((x,y)\)-space. The constrained problem may be treated using a Lagrange-multiplier function; if fewer independent variables parameterize the constraint surface, it may instead be reformulated as an unconstrained variational problem and analyzed with the Euler--Lagrange equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational constraint is holonomic if it is independent of the derivative of the dependent variable, or can be integrated into an equivalent derivative-free equation. It defines a constraint surface. One may use a Lagrange-multiplier function, or, when the surface can be parameterized by fewer independent variables, reduce the problem to an unconstrained Euler–Lagrange problem.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is independent of }y'\text{, or the original constraint is integrable to }M(x,y(x))=0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M(x,y(x))=0\text{ is holonomic; if its constraint surface admits a parameterization by fewer independent variables, the variational problem can be reduced to an unconstrained one.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Functional Annihilator Span Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation of a linear functional vanishing on the common kernel of finitely many other linear functionals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_n\) be linear functionals on a vector space \(X\). If \[\forall x\in X,\quad \bigl(f_i(x)=0\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,n\bigr)\implies f_0(x)=0,\] then there exist scalars \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\) such that \[f_0+\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i f_i=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a linear functional vanishes on the common kernel of finitely many linear functionals, it is a linear combination of those functionals.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a vector space over a scalar field}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\quad f_0+\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i f_i=0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrange Multiplier Rule for Regular Functional Equality Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity of the Lagrangian at a regular extremum subject to finitely many functional equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_0\) is an extremum of \(f\) subject to \(g_i(x)=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and \(x_0\) is a regular point of these constraints, then there exist scalars \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\) such that \[f+\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i g_i\] is stationary at \(x_0\); equivalently, for every direction \(h\), \[\delta f(x_0;h)+\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i\,\delta g_i(x_0;h)=0.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Side constraints in state-control optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines functional side constraints and their classification by dependence on controls and states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) denote a state and \(g\) a control or design parameter. Side constraints are equalities or inequalities involving scalar-valued functionals on the state and control spaces. For example, an inequality-constrained state-control problem has the form
\[
\min_{\phi,g}\mathcal J(\phi,g)\quad\text{subject to}\quad F(\phi,g)=0,\qquad \Lambda(\phi,g)\le 0.
\]
Side constraints are classified as either control-only constraints or constraints involving the state, alone or jointly with the control. An explicit bound on the control is a control-only side constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Side constraints are functional equalities or inequalities added to a state-control optimization problem. They are classified as control-only constraints or constraints involving the state, possibly together with the control. Explicit control bounds count as control-only side constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) lies in the state space and \(g\) lies in the control or design-parameter space.
\(\mathcal J\) is the objective, \(F(\phi,g)=0\) is the governing state equation, and \(\Lambda\) is a scalar-valued functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{\phi,g}\mathcal J(\phi,g)\ \text{subject to}\ F(\phi,g)=0,\ \Lambda(\phi,g)\le 0\), with side constraints classified as control-only or state-involving.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and \(H\) be continuously Fréchet differentiable near \(x_0\), with \(H(x_0)=0\), and suppose \(x_0\) is a regular point of \(H\). If \(f\) has a local extremum at \(x_0\) subject to \(H(x)=0\), then there exists \(z_0^*\in Z^*\) such that the Lagrangian \(L(x)=f(x)+z_0^*H(x)\) is stationary at \(x_0\), equivalently \(f'(x_0)+z_0^*H'(x_0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular local extremum under a smooth equality constraint, a continuous dual multiplier exists that makes the Lagrangian stationary.

children.title: Composite Constraints
children.top_down_role: Constraints with nested mappings or compositionally structured terms.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard inverse-image representation of a composite constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inverse-image formulation of a composite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a mapping \(F:X\to Y\) and a nonempty set \(D\subset Y\), the composite constraint generated by \((F,D)\) is
\[F(x)\in D.\]
Its feasible set and extended-real indicator representation are
\[C:=F^{-1}(D)=\{x\in X:F(x)\in D\},\qquad \delta_C(x)=\delta_D(F(x)),\]
where \(\delta_D(y)=0\) for \(y\in D\) and \(\delta_D(y)=+\infty\) otherwise. Thus minimizing an objective over \(C\) is equivalent, at the level of feasible minimizers, to minimizing its sum with \(\delta_D\circ F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite constraint requires a mapping value to belong to a prescribed set; its feasible-set indicator is the composition of that set’s indicator with the mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically correct, internally consistent, and appropriate for the Composite Constraints leaf, but it has no citation with an inspectable locator. The standard-field rationale is insufficient to satisfy the statement-review citation requirement.

children.title: Nonsmooth Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Constraint representations requiring generalized differential objects.

assumptions_latex: \(G:X\to Y\) and \(Q:X\rightrightarrows Y\) are given mappings.

notation.meaning: Solution set of the generalized equation
Set-valued part of the constraint system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-equation representation of finite-dimensional nonsmooth constraints.

source_refs.locator: 5.2.2 Variational Systems as Equilibrium Constraints p. 51
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite-dimensional nonsmooth constraint system in generalized-equation form is
\[0\in G(x)+Q(x),\]
with solution set
\[S:=\{x\in X:0\in G(x)+Q(x)\}.\]
The set-valued mapping \(Q\) can encode nonsmooth or geometric restrictions. For example, if \(H:X\to Y\) and \(D\subset Y\) is nonempty, then the composite constraint \(H(x)\in D\) is equivalently written as
\[0\in H(x)+(-D).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional nonsmooth constraint system can be represented by a generalized equation whose set-valued term encodes nonsmooth or geometric restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Constraint Systems

children.title: Composite-Calculus Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Multiplier representations shaped by compositional structure.

assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, with \(g(F(\bar x))<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq \nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(F(\bar x))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard limiting-subdifferential chain rule under a horizon qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential chain rule for a smooth inner mapping at a finite composite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and lower semicontinuous with \(g(F(\bar x))<+\infty\). If
\[\partial^\infty g(F(\bar x))\cap\ker \nabla F(\bar x)^\top=\{0\},\]
then
\[\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\subseteq \nabla F(\bar x)^\top\partial g(F(\bar x)).\]
Thus every limiting subgradient in \(\partial(g\circ F)(\bar x)\) has the form \(\nabla F(\bar x)^\top y^*\) for some \(y^*\in\partial g(F(\bar x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a finite composite value, the horizon qualification gives the limiting-subdifferential chain-rule inclusion and an adjoint multiplier representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Calculus Interfaces

children.title: Separation Principles
children.top_down_role: Convex-geometric separation routes to dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists u\ne0,\alpha\in\mathbb{R}:\sup_{a\in A}\langle u,a\rangle<\alpha<\inf_{b\in B}\langle u,b\rangle\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-dimensional strong separation theorem for a compact convex set and a disjoint closed convex set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty disjoint convex sets, with \(A\) compact and \(B\) closed. Then there exist \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) such that
\[\sup_{a\in A}\langle u,a\rangle<\alpha<\inf_{b\in B}\langle u,b\rangle.\]
Thus the affine hyperplane \(\{x:\langle u,x\rangle=\alpha\}\) strictly separates the two sets. The vector \(u\) supplies a nonzero dual direction from which multiplier or infeasibility certificates may be constructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint convex sets are strictly separable when one is compact and the other closed, producing a nonzero dual separating direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Principles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional strong-separation theorem is correctly stated, its hypotheses are sufficient, and theorem is the appropriate content kind. No source citation or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Alternative Principles
children.top_down_role: Mutually exclusive primal-feasibility and dual-certificate systems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Exactly one of }\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\}\ne\varnothing\text{ and }\{y\in\mathbb{R}^m:A^\top y\ge 0,\ b^\top y<0\}\ne\varnothing\text{ holds.}\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas alternative for equality constraints with nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), exactly one of the following systems is solvable:
\[Ax=b,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad x\ge0,\]
or
\[A^\top y\ge0,\qquad b^\top y<0,\qquad y\in\mathbb{R}^m.\]
All vector inequalities are componentwise. The second system is the alternative certificate for failure of the first system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly one holds: the right-hand side is a nonnegative combination of the matrix columns, or a dual vector strictly certifies that it is not.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Principles

children.title: Dual-Certificate Generation
children.top_down_role: Construction of multiplier candidates from convex-geometric certificates.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}=\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: directly checkable Farkas infeasibility certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional certificate for nonnegative linear feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). A vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfying
\[A^\top y\ge0,\qquad b^\top y<0\]
is a dual certificate that
\[\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}=\varnothing.\]
The certificate is directly checkable from the two displayed inequalities and is generated by the corresponding Farkas alternative whenever the primal system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector with nonnegative transpose product and negative pairing with the right-hand side is a directly checkable certificate of infeasibility for a nonnegative linear system.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Certificate Generation

children.title: Separation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex or nonclosed settings limiting classical separation routes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{dist}(A,B)=0\), and no affine hyperplane strongly separates \(A\) and \(B\) with a positive margin.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit zero-distance closed-convex example showing failure of positive-margin separation without compactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of positive-margin strong separation for unbounded closed convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sets
\[A:=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:t\ge e^s\},\qquad B:=\{(s,0):s\in\mathbb{R}\}\]
are nonempty, closed, convex, disjoint, and unbounded, and they satisfy
\[\operatorname{dist}(A,B)=0.\]
They admit no affine-hyperplane separation with a positive strict margin. This is a failure boundary for the compact-versus-closed strong-separation theorem when compactness is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two disjoint unbounded closed convex sets can have zero distance and fail to admit affine-hyperplane separation with a positive strict margin.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Failure Regimes

children.title: Normal-Cone Calculus Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Generation through normals to intersections and inverse images.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) is closed convex, \(F(x)=Ax+b\), and \(F(\bar x)\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\cap_iC_i}(\bar x)=\sum_iN_{C_i}(\bar x)\) and \(N_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x)=A^\top N_D(F(\bar x))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard qualified convex normal-cone rules for intersections and affine inverse images
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified convex normal-cone calculus in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\bar x\in\bigcap_{i=1}^p C_i\), the relative-interior qualification \(\bigcap_{i=1}^p\operatorname{ri}C_i\ne\varnothing\) yields
\[N_{\cap_{i=1}^pC_i}(\bar x)=\sum_{i=1}^pN_{C_i}(\bar x).\]
For an affine mapping \(F(x)=Ax+b\), a closed convex set \(D\), and \(\bar x\in F^{-1}(D)\), the stated inverse-image qualification yields
\[N_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x)=A^\top N_D(F(\bar x)).\]
These identities generate normal multipliers for intersected constraints and composite affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under relative-interior qualifications, normals to intersections add, while normals to affine inverse images are adjoint images of normals to the target set.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Calculus Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Both qualified convex normal-cone identities are mathematically consistent with the finite-dimensional role of this topic, and property is an acceptable kind for these calculus identities. The record lacks a source citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Extremal-Principle Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Nonconvex multiplier generation through extremal set systems.

assumptions_latex: The family \(\{\Omega_i\}_{i=1}^p\) is locally extremal at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x_i^*\in N_{\Omega_i}(\bar x):\sum_i x_i^*=0,\ \sum_i\|x_i^*\|=1\).

notation.meaning: Limiting normal cone to a set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-normal form of the extremal principle.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.3 Extremal Principle in Finite Dimensions p. 178
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the locally closed sets \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_p\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) form a locally extremal system at their common point \(\bar x\), then there exist limiting normals
\[x_i^*\in N_{\Omega_i}(\bar x),\qquad i=1,\ldots,p,\]
satisfying the balance and nontriviality conditions
\[\sum_{i=1}^p x_i^*=0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^p\|x_i^*\|=1.\]
Thus local geometric extremality produces a normalized family of nonzero dual objects without requiring convexity of the sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local extremality of a finite nonconvex set system generates normalized limiting normals whose sum is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Extremal-Principle Mechanisms

children.title: Constraint-Regularity Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Multiplier generation from stability properties of constraint systems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D)\) locally for some \(\kappa>0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard metric-subregularity error-bound condition for a composite constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error-bound form of constraint regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The composite constraint \(F(x)\in D\) is metrically subregular at the feasible point \(\bar x\) if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U,\]
where \(C:=F^{-1}(D)\). This condition quantitatively converts residual size in the image space into distance from feasibility and is the regularity mechanism used in local penalty estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint regularity is expressed by a local error bound that controls distance to feasibility by the constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Regularity Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local error-bound inequality is a correct finite-dimensional metric-subregularity condition and fits the Constraint-Regularity Mechanisms leaf. No source citation with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Exact-Penalty Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Multiplier generation through locally exact penalized formulations.

assumptions_latex: \(C:=F^{-1}(D)\), and \(\bar x\in C\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\bar\rho\ge0\ \exists U\ni\bar x\ \forall\rho\ge\bar\rho\ \forall x\in U:\ P_\rho(\bar x)\le P_\rho(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard local exact-penalty definition using the distance residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local distance-penalty exactness for composite constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[P_\rho(x):=f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D),\qquad \rho\ge0.\]
This penalty is locally exact at the feasible constrained local minimizer \(\bar x\) if there exist \(\bar\rho\ge0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that, for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\),
\[P_\rho(\bar x)\le P_\rho(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U.\]
The infimum of all admissible thresholds \(\bar\rho\) is the local exact-penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual penalty is locally exact at a constrained local minimizer when every sufficiently large penalty parameter makes that point a local minimizer of the penalized objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty Mechanisms

children.title: Regularity-to-Penalty Transfer
children.top_down_role: Connections between constraint stability and penalty exactness.

assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in C\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\), and \(C\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\).
\(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) with constant \(L\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\rho>L\kappa:\ \bar x\text{ locally minimizes }x\mapsto f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D).\)

notation.meaning: Local Lipschitz constant of the objective

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard transfer from a local error bound and objective Lipschitz continuity to distance-penalty exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative transfer from metric subregularity to local exact penalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty, and set \(C:=F^{-1}(D)\). Suppose \(\bar x\in C\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\), the set \(C\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\), and \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\) with constant \(L\ge0\). If, for some \(\kappa>0\),
\[\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D)\]
holds locally near \(\bar x\), then for every \(\rho>L\kappa\), the point \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of
\[x\longmapsto f(x)+\rho\operatorname{dist}(F(x),D).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz objective, a local constraint error bound transfers a constrained local minimum to the distance-penalized problem whenever the penalty parameter exceeds the product of the two moduli.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularity-to-Penalty Transfer

children.title: Penalty-Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where penalization fails to preserve local solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near a feasible local minimizer \(\bar x\).
The feasible set \(S\) satisfies \(d(x,S)\leq \kappa r(x)\) locally, where \(r\geq0\) vanishes exactly on \(S\).
\(f\) has local Lipschitz modulus at most \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f(x)+\rho r(x)\) whenever \(\rho>L\kappa\); without a local error bound of this form, no finite exact-penalty threshold follows in general.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz-error-bound boundary for scalar exact penalties.

source_refs.locator: 5.4.3 Linear Suboptimality for Minimization Problems p. 125
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x:r(x)=0\}\), and suppose \(\bar x\in S\) locally minimizes \(f\). If \(|f(x)-f(z)|\leq L\|x-z\|\) near \(\bar x\) and \(d(x,S)\leq\kappa r(x)\) locally, then every \(\rho>L\kappa\) makes \(\bar x\) a local minimizer of \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho r(x)\). Thus Lipschitz growth combined with a linear feasibility error bound yields finite exactness. If such an error bound fails, arbitrarily small infeasibility may dominate every fixed linear penalty, so finite exactness is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz objective and linear feasibility error bound give exact penalization above a computable threshold; without the error bound, finite exactness may fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Exactness Boundaries

\(\bar x\) is a local minimizer subject to \(h_j(x)=0\) and \(g_i(x)\leq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), and \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \( ar x\) be a local minimizer. Then there exist \(\lambda_0\geq0\), \(\mu\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), not all zero, such that \[\lambda_0
abla f( ar x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j
abla h_j( ar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x)=0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i( ar x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]

children.title: Geometric Fritz John Forms
children.top_down_role: Multiplier rules expressed through feasible-set geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(C\subset\mathbb R^q\) is closed, and \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) subject to \(F(x)\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There are \(\lambda_0\geq0\) and \(y^*\in N_C(F(\bar x))\), not both zero, satisfying \(\lambda_0\nabla f(\bar x)+DF(\bar x)^*y^*=0\).

notation.meaning: limiting normal cone to the closed constraint set
adjoint derivative of the constraint mapping

source_refs.locator: 5.1.1 Minimization Problems with Geometric Constraints p. 4
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(F(x)\in C\), and let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer. Under the finite-dimensional geometric extremal rule applicable to this smooth inverse-image system, there exist \(\lambda_0\geq0\) and \(y^*\in N_C(F(\bar x))\), not both zero, such that \[\lambda_0\nabla f(\bar x)+DF(\bar x)^*y^*=0.\] The case \(\lambda_0>0\) is normal and can be scaled to \(\lambda_0=1\); the case \(\lambda_0=0\) is abnormal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A geometric constraint yields an objective multiplier and a normal to the target set whose derivative pullback balances the objective gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Fritz John Forms

children.title: Conic Fritz John Forms
children.top_down_role: Multiplier rules for cone-valued constraint systems.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\).
\(K\subset\mathbb R^q\) is a closed convex cone, and \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f\) subject to \(G(x)\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(\lambda_0\geq0\) and \(y^*\in K^\circ\), not both zero, with stationarity and cone complementarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-convex-cone specialization with negative-polar multipliers.

source_refs.locator: 5.1.1 Minimization Problems with Geometric Constraints p. 4
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(G(x)\in K\), let \(\bar x\) be a local minimizer. The conic Fritz John system consists of \(\lambda_0\geq0\) and \(y^*\in K^\circ\), not both zero, satisfying \[\lambda_0\nabla f(\bar x)+DG(\bar x)^*y^*=0,\qquad \langle y^*,G(\bar x)\rangle=0.\] Equivalently, \(y^*\in N_K(G(\bar x))\). This formulation fixes the negative-polar convention; using the positive dual cone reverses the sign of the multiplier term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex conic constraint, Fritz John stationarity uses a polar-cone multiplier orthogonal to the feasible cone value.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Fritz John Forms

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fritz John conditions for differentiable scalar inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar-inequality specialization of the conic Fritz John multiplier rule, requiring no constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose $\bar x\in\operatorname{int}C$ is a local minimizer of $f(x)$ subject to $g_i(x)\le0$ for $i=1,\ldots,m$, and let $I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}$. If $f$ and every $g_i$ with $i\in I(\bar x)$ are differentiable at $\bar x$, then there exist $\lambda_0\ge0$ and $\lambda_i\ge0$ for $i\in I(\bar x)$, not all zero, such that $$\lambda_0\nabla f(\bar x)+\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x)=0.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every interior local minimizer of the differentiable scalar-inequality problem has nontrivial nonnegative Fritz John multipliers satisfying stationarity over the objective and active constraints.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ and }g_i\ (i\in I(\bar x))\text{ are differentiable at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\exists\lambda_0\ge0,\ \exists(\lambda_i)_{i\in I( ar x)}\ge0:\ (\lambda_0,(\lambda_i)_{i\in I( ar x)})
e0,\quad \lambda_0
abla f( ar x)+\sum_{i\in I( ar x)}\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x)=0.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional normal-cone formula under MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p,\ g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where every \(h_j\) and \(g_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in\Gamma\). If MFCQ holds at \(\bar x\), then \[N_\Gamma(\bar x)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j\nabla h_j(\bar x)+\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x):\mu\in\mathbb R^p,\ \lambda_i\geq0\right\},\] where \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\) and \(N_\Gamma\) is the limiting normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, the limiting normal cone to the smooth feasible set consists exactly of equality-gradient combinations plus nonnegative combinations of active inequality gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(h_j,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_\Gamma(\bar x)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j\nabla h_j(\bar x)+\sum_{i\in I(\bar x)}\lambda_i\nabla g_i(\bar x):\mu\in\mathbb R^p,\ \lambda_i\geq0\right\}.\]

notation.meaning: limiting normal cone to the feasible set

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the negative polar \(K^\circ=\{z:\langle z,k\rangle\leq0\text{ for every }k\in K\}\), the normal cone to a closed convex cone satisfies \[N_K(y)=\{z\in K^\circ:\langle z,y\rangle=0\}=K^\circ\cap y^\perp\qquad(y\in K).\] Consequently, membership of a conic multiplier in \(N_K(y)\) is equivalent to dual feasibility \(z\in K^\circ\) together with complementarity \(\langle z,y\rangle=0\). Under the positive-dual convention, the corresponding multiplier is \(-z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal to a convex cone is precisely a polar-cone vector complementary to the cone point, linking geometric normals with dual multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-objective-multiplier branch of smooth Fritz John systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), and \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where the functions are continuously differentiable near the feasible point \( ar x\). A nonzero Fritz John multiplier tuple \((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) is normal when \(\lambda_0>0\). Its normalized multipliers \(\widehat\mu=\mu/\lambda_0\) and \(\widehat\lambda=\lambda/\lambda_0\) satisfy \[
abla f( ar x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\widehat\mu_j
abla h_j( ar x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\widehat\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x)=0,\qquad \widehat\lambda_i\geq0,\qquad \widehat\lambda_i g_i( ar x)=0.\] Thus every normal Fritz John tuple determines a KKT tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Fritz John tuple with positive objective multiplier can be divided by that multiplier to obtain KKT multipliers with objective multiplier one.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h_j,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(\bar x\).
\((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) is a nonzero Fritz John multiplier tuple at \(\bar x\) with \(\lambda_0>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normalized tuple \(\left(1,\mu/\lambda_0,\lambda/\lambda_0\right)\) satisfies the KKT stationarity, sign, and complementarity conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Abnormal Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-objective-multiplier branch marking failure of KKT normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), and \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where the functions are continuously differentiable near the feasible point \( ar x\). A nonzero Fritz John tuple \((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) is abnormal when \(\lambda_0=0\). It then satisfies \[\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j
abla h_j( ar x)+\sum_{i\in I( ar x)}\lambda_i
abla g_i( ar x)=0,\qquad \lambda_i\geq0,\qquad (\mu,\lambda)
eq0,\] where \(I( ar x)=\{i:g_i( ar x)=0\}\). No positive scaling of this tuple can produce an objective multiplier equal to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An abnormal Fritz John tuple has zero objective multiplier and a nontrivial homogeneous dependence among equality and active-inequality gradients, so it cannot be normalized to a KKT tuple.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h_j,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(\bar x\).
\((0,\mu,\lambda)\) is a nonzero Fritz John multiplier tuple at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint multipliers satisfy a nontrivial homogeneous active-gradient relation, and no positive scaling yields objective multiplier \(1\).

assumptions_latex: \((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) satisfies a positively homogeneous Fritz John system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rescaling \((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\mapsto(1,\mu/\lambda_0,\lambda/\lambda_0)\) preserves feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous rescaling from Fritz John to KKT multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) satisfies the Fritz John equations, then \((t\lambda_0,t\mu,t\lambda)\) satisfies them for every \(t>0\). When \(\lambda_0>0\), choosing \(t=1/\lambda_0\) produces the equivalent normalized tuple \[(1,\widehat\mu,\widehat\lambda)=\left(1,\frac{\mu}{\lambda_0},\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_0}\right).\] Sign restrictions and complementary slackness are invariant under this positive scaling. When \(\lambda_0=0\), no positive scaling reaches the normalized hyperplane \(\lambda_0=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive homogeneity permits transition from a normal Fritz John tuple to a KKT tuple, while the abnormal branch cannot cross to objective multiplier one.

knowledge_statements.title: Qualification-Controlled Normality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MFCQ exclusion of abnormal smooth nonlinear-programming multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,p\), and \(g_i(x)\leq0\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), where the functions are continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(\bar x\). If MFCQ holds at \(\bar x\), then every nonzero Fritz John multiplier tuple \((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) at \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\lambda_0>0\). Consequently, every such tuple can be positively rescaled to a KKT tuple with objective multiplier \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth equality-and-inequality constrained problem, MFCQ excludes nonzero abnormal Fritz John multipliers and therefore permits KKT normalization.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h_j,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are continuously differentiable near a feasible point \(\bar x\).
\((\lambda_0,\mu,\lambda)\) is a nonzero Fritz John multiplier tuple at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_0>0\), and \(\left(1,\mu/\lambda_0,\lambda/\lambda_0\right)\) is a normalized KKT tuple.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant Rank Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric constraints differentiated with respect to the lower-level variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: CRCQ holds at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ if there exists an open neighborhood $U$ of $(\bar x,\bar y)$ such that, for every $I\subseteq\{i:g_i(\bar x,\bar y)=0\}$, the family $\{\nabla_y g_i(x,y):i\in I\}$ has constant rank on $U$.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni(\bar x,\bar y)\ \forall I\subseteq\{i:g_i(\bar x,\bar y)=0\}:\ \operatorname{rank}\{\nabla_y g_i(x,y):i\in I\}\text{ is constant on }U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relations between Cottle and Slater qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One unconditional implication and a converse requiring convexity of every constraint function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the problem satisfies the Cottle constraint qualification at some \(x\in S\), then it satisfies the Slater constraint qualification. Conversely, if every \(g_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), is convex and the problem satisfies the Slater constraint qualification, then it satisfies the Cottle constraint qualification at every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cottle qualification at some feasible point implies Slater qualification. If all constraint functions are convex, Slater qualification implies Cottle qualification at every feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \text{First implication: Cottle qualification holds at some }x\in S
\text{Converse: }g_i\text{ is convex for every }i=1,\ldots,m\text{ and Slater qualification holds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\exists x\in S:\operatorname{Cottle}(x)]\Rightarrow\operatorname{Slater},\qquad [\operatorname{Slater}\land(\forall i,\ g_i\text{ convex})]\Rightarrow[\forall x\in S,\operatorname{Cottle}(x)]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extended MFCQ Characterizes Bounded Multiplier Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth, not necessarily convex, semi-infinite programming at a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x_0 be a locally optimal solution of a semi-infinite program in \mathbb{R}^n. Suppose f and g(\cdot,\omega), \omega\in\Omega, are continuously differentiable and (x,\omega)\mapsto\nabla_x g(x,\omega) is continuous. Then \Lambda(x_0) is nonempty and bounded if and only if extended MFCQ holds. If extended MFCQ holds, then \Lambda_m(x_0) is nonempty and bounded for every m\ge n. Conversely, if m\ge n+1 and \Lambda_m(x_0) is nonempty and bounded, then extended MFCQ holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer of a smooth semi-infinite program, extended MFCQ is equivalent to nonemptiness and boundedness of the full measure-valued multiplier set. It implies the same properties for discrete multiplier sets with at least n atoms; the discrete converse requires at least n+1 atoms.
assumptions_latex: x_0\text{ is a locally optimal solution of a not necessarily convex semi-infinite program in }\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
[\Lambda(x_0)
e\varnothing	ext{ and }\Lambda(x_0)	ext{ is bounded}]\iff\operatorname{EMFCQ}(x_0);\quad \operatorname{EMFCQ}(x_0)\Rightarrow[\Lambda_m(x_0)
e\varnothing	ext{ and bounded for every }m\ge n];\quad [m\ge n+1,\ \Lambda_m(x_0)
e\varnothing	ext{ and bounded}]\Rightarrow\operatorname{EMFCQ}(x_0).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-dependent strict constraint qualification for a smooth inequality- and equality-constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For $\min\{f(x):g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}$, SMFCQ holds at $x^0$ if there is a Lagrange multiplier $(\lambda,\mu)$ satisfying $\lambda\ge0$, $\lambda^	op g(x^0)=0$, and
\[

abla f(x^0)+\lambda^	op
abla g(x^0)+\mu^	op
abla h(x^0)=0,
\]
and a direction $d$ such that $
abla g_i(x^0)d<0$ for every $i\in I(x^0)\setminus J(\lambda)$, $
abla g_i(x^0)d=0$ for every $i\in J(\lambda)$, and $
abla h_j(x^0)d=0$ for $j=1,\ldots,q$, while $\{
abla g_i(x^0):i\in J(\lambda)\}\cup\{
abla h_j(x^0):j=1,\ldots,q\}$ is linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SMFCQ requires a KKT multiplier and a direction tangent to the equalities and the inequalities indexed by the multiplier set, strictly decreasing the remaining active inequalities, together with independence of the multiplier-indexed inequality gradients and equality gradients.
assumptions_latex: x^0\text{ is a point for }\min\{f(x):g(x)\le0,\ h(x)=0\}.
I(x^0)=\{i:g_i(x^0)=0\},\quad J(\lambda)\text{ is the multiplier-dependent index set used in the formulation.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SMFCQ}(x^0)\text{ holds exactly when the stated multiplier, directional, and gradient-independence requirements are satisfied.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Suboptimality under the Mangasarian–Fromovitz Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nearby approximate KKT stationarity for an epsilon-optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be an Asplund space, let \(\varepsilon>0\), and let \(\Omega=X\). Assume that \(\varphi_0\) is locally Lipschitz on the set of \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solutions and that \(\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_{m+r}\) are strictly differentiable and satisfy MFCQ on that set. Then, for every \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution \(\bar x\) and every \(v>0\), there exist an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution \(\widehat x\), a subgradient \(x_0^*\in\partial\varphi_0(\widehat x)\), and multipliers \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{m+r}\) such that \(\|\widehat x-\bar x\|\le v\), \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(\lambda_i\varphi_i(\widehat x)=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and \[\left\|x_0^*+\sum_{i=1}^{m+r}\lambda_i\nabla\varphi_i(\widehat x)\right\|\le\frac{\varepsilon}{v}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective is locally Lipschitz and the strictly differentiable constraints satisfy MFCQ throughout the epsilon-optimal set, every epsilon-optimal point has a nearby epsilon-optimal point satisfying inequality-multiplier nonnegativity, complementarity, and an approximate KKT residual bounded by epsilon divided by the permitted displacement.
assumptions_latex: \varphi_0\text{ is locally Lipschitz on the set of }\varepsilon\text{-optimal solutions}
\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_{m+r}\text{ are strictly differentiable and satisfy MFCQ on that set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\widehat x,x_0^*,\lambda:\ \widehat x\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-optimal},\ \|\widehat x-\bar x\|\le v,\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \lambda_i\varphi_i(\widehat x)=0\ (1\le i\le m),\ \left\|x_0^*+\sum_{i=1}^{m+r}\lambda_i\nabla\varphi_i(\widehat x)\right\|\le\varepsilon/v

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification for inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the inequality-only MFCQ at a feasible point; no equality constraints occur in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible point $\bar x$ with active set $I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}$, the Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification holds if there exists $d\in\mathbf E$ such that $$\langle\nabla g_i(\bar x),d\rangle<0\qquad\text{for every }i\in I(\bar x).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ holds at a feasible point when one direction strictly decreases the linearization of every active inequality constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant Rank Constraint Qualification and Its Basic Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: CRCQ along the feasible set, together with the stated polyhedral case, qualification implications, and VI multiplier consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For $x\in K$, CRCQ holds at $x$ if there exists a neighborhood $\mathcal N$ of $x$ such that, for every $\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal I(x)$ and $\mathcal J'\subseteq\{1,\ldots,\ell\}$, the family
\[
\{\nabla g_i(x'):i\in\mathcal I'\}\cup\{\nabla h_j(x'):j\in\mathcal J'\}
\]
has a rank depending only on $(\mathcal I',\mathcal J')$ for all $x'\in K\cap\mathcal N$. CRCQ holds at every feasible point when all constraint functions are affine. Moreover, $\mathrm{LICQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{CRCQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{KTCQ}$. If CRCQ holds at a solution $x$ of $\operatorname{VI}(K,F)$, then $\mathcal M(x)\ne\varnothing$, although $\mathcal M(x)$ may be unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CRCQ requires every selected subfamily of active inequality and equality gradients to have locally constant rank along the feasible set. It holds for polyhedral systems, is implied by LICQ, implies KTCQ, and guarantees existence—but not boundedness—of VI multipliers at a solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globality of MFCQ for Convex-Affine Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification for convex differentiable inequalities and affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and continuously differentiable for $i=1,\ldots,m$, let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{\ell}$ be affine, and let $K$ be the associated feasible set. MFCQ holds at one point of $K$ if and only if it holds at every point of $K$. In particular, if $\ell=0$ and $K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g(x)\le0\}$, then MFCQ holds at a point of $K$ if and only if there exists $\widehat x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying $g(\widehat x)<0$ componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex differentiable inequalities and affine equalities, MFCQ holds at one feasible point exactly when it holds at every feasible point. Without equalities, this is equivalent to strict feasibility of all inequalities.
assumptions_latex: g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and continuously differentiable for }i=1,\ldots,m
K\text{ is the associated feasible set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists x\in K:\operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\bigr)\iff\bigl(\forall x\in K:\operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\bigr),\qquad \ell=0\Rightarrow\left[\bigl(\exists x\in K:\operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\bigr)\iff\bigl(\exists\widehat x:g(\widehat x)<0\bigr)\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Directional Slater Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and comparison with the weaker aggregate directional inequality for a max-represented convex component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X=\{x\mid g(x)-h(x)\le0\}, let \bar x\in X satisfy g(\bar x)=h(\bar x), and suppose h=\max_{i\in\mathcal I}h_i with differentiable convex h_i. Writing \mathcal M_h(\bar x)=\{i\mid h_i(\bar x)=h(\bar x)\}, the pointwise directional Slater condition holds at \bar x if there exists \bar v such that g'(\bar x;\bar v)<\nabla h_i(\bar x)^\top\bar v for every i\in\mathcal M_h(\bar x). Equivalently, g'(\bar x;\bar v)<\min_{i\in\mathcal M_h(\bar x)}\nabla h_i(\bar x)^\top\bar v. This condition implies g'(\bar x;\bar v)<h'(\bar x;\bar v), but the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an active DC constraint g−h≤0 with h represented as the maximum of differentiable convex pieces, pointwise directional Slater requires one direction that strictly satisfies the linearization associated with every active piece. It implies strict inequality against the directional derivative of h, whereas that aggregate inequality need not imply the pointwise condition.
assumptions_latex: h=\max_{i\in\mathcal I}h_i\text{ with each }h_i\text{ convex and differentiable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar v\ \forall i\in\mathcal M_h(\bar x):\ g'(\bar x;\bar v)<\nabla h_i(\bar x)^\top\bar v\iff g'(\bar x;\bar v)<\min_{i\in\mathcal M_h(\bar x)}\nabla h_i(\bar x)^\top\bar v,\quad\text{and this implies }g'(\bar x;\bar v)<h'(\bar x;\bar v)\text{ but not conversely.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LICQ Ensures Unique Lagrange Multipliers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear programming; the source calls linear independence of the active constraint gradients regularity condition A and contrasts it with Slater-type regularity B.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a solution \(x^*\), if the gradients of all active inequality constraints and all equality constraints are linearly independent, then the Lagrange multiplier vector associated with the first-order conditions is unique. By contrast, Slater-type regularity alone need not imply multiplier uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear independence of the active constraint gradients makes the NLP Lagrange multipliers unique, whereas Slater regularity alone does not guarantee uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The Lagrange multiplier vector at }x^*\text{ is unique; Slater regularity alone is not sufficient.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of Barrier-Equation Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability and domain result for the barrier equation associated with a convexly constrained monotone VI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be defined by (12.7.23), with every \(g_i\) convex and continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous and monotone on \(K\). Assume \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\) is nonempty and compact. If \(\eta=0\), assume Slater's constraint qualification for \(K\); if \(\eta>0\), assume \(F\) is continuous and monotone on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), equation (12.7.24) has at least one solution and every such solution belongs to \(\operatorname{dom}g_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convexity, compact-solvability, and eta-dependent qualification assumptions, every positive barrier parameter gives a solvable barrier equation, and all its solutions lie in the barrier domain.
assumptions_latex: g_i\text{ is convex and }C^1\text{ on }\mathbb{R}^n\text{ for every }i
F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is continuous and monotone on }K
\eta>0\Rightarrow F\text{ is continuous and monotone on }\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0,\quad \operatorname{SOL}(\text{equation (12.7.24)})\ne\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{SOL}(\text{equation (12.7.24)})\subseteq\operatorname{dom}g_\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Slater Tangent-Cone Formula for a Max-Represented DC Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tangent-cone characterization under pointwise directional Slater.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid g(x)-h(x)\le0\}, where g and h are convex and h=\max_{i\in\mathcal I}h_i with differentiable convex h_i. Let \bar x\in X satisfy g(\bar x)=h(\bar x). If there exists \bar v such that g'(\bar x;\bar v)<\nabla h_i(\bar x)^\top\bar v for every i\in\mathcal M_h(\bar x), then \mathcal T(\bar x;X)=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid g'(\bar x;v)-h'(\bar x;v)\le0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an active DC inequality whose subtracted convex term is the maximum of finitely many differentiable convex pieces, pointwise directional Slater guarantees that the tangent cone is exactly the set of directions with nonpositive directional derivative of g−h.
assumptions_latex: h=\max_{i\in\mathcal I}h_i\text{ with each }h_i\text{ convex and differentiable}
\exists\bar v\ \forall i\in\mathcal M_h(\bar x):\ g'(\bar x;\bar v)<\nabla h_i(\bar x)^\top\bar v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T(\bar x;X)=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid g'(\bar x;v)-h'(\bar x;v)\le0\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Convex Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-valued convex inequalities with affine equalities in Euclidean space.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^s\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(Ax^s=b\) and \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Slater Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine conic feasibility with a solid closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let \(K\subset Y\) be a closed convex cone with nonempty interior, let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(b\in Y\). For the affine conic system \[b-Ax\in K,\] the conic Slater condition holds if there exists \(x^s\in X\) such that \[b-Ax^s\in\operatorname{int}K.\] Equivalently, \((b-A(X))\cap\operatorname{int}K\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conic Slater qualification requires a feasible point whose affine conic slack lies in the topological interior of the cone.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
\(K\subset Y\) is a closed convex cone with nonempty interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^s\in X\) such that \(b-Ax^s\in\operatorname{int}K\).

notation.meaning: Conic slack associated with a point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasi-relative-interior variant for cones with possibly empty topological interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the quasi-relative interior by \[\operatorname{qri}K=\{y\in K:\overline{\operatorname{cone}}(K-y)\ \text{is a linear subspace of }Y\}.\] A generalized function-space Slater condition for \(b-Ax\in K\) is the existence of \(x^s\in X\) such that \[b-Ax^s\in\operatorname{qri}K.\] This replaces topological interior by a generalized interior that can remain nonempty when \(K\) has empty interior in the ambient infinite-dimensional topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function-space Slater variant places a feasible conic slack in the cone's quasi-relative interior when ordinary interior is empty.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty convex set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), its relative interior is \[\operatorname{ri}C=\{x\in C:\exists\varepsilon>0,\ B_\varepsilon(x)\cap\operatorname{aff}C\subset C\}.\] The relative-interior qualification for two convex constraints \(x\in C\) and \(x\in D\) is \[\operatorname{ri}C\cap\operatorname{ri}D\ne\varnothing.\] The condition measures interiority within each set's affine hull and therefore remains meaningful when either set has empty ambient interior.

notation.meaning: Algebraic interior of a convex set.
Constraint sets whose intersection is under consideration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic-interior qualification independent of a chosen topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The algebraic interior, or core, of \(C\) is \[\operatorname{core}C=\{x\in C:\forall d\in X\ \exists\varepsilon_d>0\ \forall |t|<\varepsilon_d,\ x+td\in C\}.\] A core qualification for the pair of convex constraints \(x\in C\) and \(x\in D\) is \[\operatorname{core}C\cap D\ne\varnothing.\] Thus one constraint set contains a feasible point admitting sufficiently short displacements in every algebraic direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A core qualification requires a common feasible point lying in the algebraic interior of one convex constraint set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of algebraic core is standard, but no source supports the asymmetric condition core(C) intersect D as the intended qualification rather than another core-based intersection variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Dimensional Convex Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative Slater condition on a lower-dimensional convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(g_i:C\to\mathbb{R}\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), be convex, let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be linear, and let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\). The lower-dimensional Slater condition for \[x\in C,\qquad Ax=b,\qquad g_i(x)\le0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m)\] holds if there exists \(x^s\in\operatorname{ri}C\) such that \[Ax^s=b,\qquad g_i(x^s)<0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Interiority is taken relative to \(\operatorname{aff}C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-dimensional convex system satisfies relative Slater qualification when a point in the relative interior of its domain satisfies every affine equality and every convex inequality strictly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x^s\in\operatorname{ri}C\) such that \(Ax^s=b\) and \(g_i(x^s)<0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex set \(S\subset X\), define \[\operatorname{sqri}S=\{x\in S:\operatorname{cone}(S-x)\ \text{is a closed linear subspace of }X\}.\] An infinite-dimensional interior-surrogate qualification for the pair \(C,D\) is \[0\in\operatorname{sqri}(C-D).\] This condition substitutes a closed linearity property of the generated cone for nonempty topological interior, which frequently fails in function spaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition relative to a specified Lagrange multiplier and its reduced constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \lambda_0\in\Lambda_0(x_0,u_0), set y_0:=G(x_0,u_0), and define K_0:=\{y\in K:\langle\lambda_0,y-y_0\rangle=0\}. The multiplier \lambda_0 satisfies the strict constraint qualification if 0\in\operatorname{int}\bigl(y_0+D_xG(x_0,u_0)X-K_0\bigr). Since K_0\subset K, strict constraint qualification implies Robinson's constraint qualification. If K is a convex cone and \langle\lambda_0,y_0\rangle=0, then K_0=K\cap\ker\lambda_0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier satisfies strict constraint qualification when Robinson's interior condition holds for its multiplier-exposed reduced constraint set. This implies ordinary Robinson qualification. For a convex cone under complementarity, the reduced set is the intersection of the cone with the multiplier's kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_0\text{ satisfies strict CQ}\iff 0\in\operatorname{int}\bigl(y_0+D_xG(x_0,u_0)X-K_0\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Uniqueness and Stability under Strict Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward consequences and a closed-cone converse for strict constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \lambda_0 satisfies the first-order optimality conditions and strict constraint qualification. Then \Lambda_0=\{\lambda_0\}, and \Omega is upper Lipschitzian at \bigl(D_xf(x_0,u_0),y_0\bigr). Conversely, let \mathcal Q(x_0):=D_xG(x_0,u_0)X+\mathcal R_{K_0}(y_0). If \Lambda_0=\{\lambda_0\} and the cones \mathcal Q(x_0) and \mathcal R_{N_K(y_0)}(\lambda_0) are closed, then strict constraint qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict constraint qualification at a first-order multiplier implies uniqueness of that multiplier and upper Lipschitz stability of the auxiliary mapping. Conversely, multiplier uniqueness implies strict qualification when the two specified cones are closed.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the converse: }\Lambda_0=\{\lambda_0\},\ \mathcal Q(x_0)\text{ and }\mathcal R_{N_K(y_0)}(\lambda_0)\text{ are closed cones}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Directional Epiderivative Chain Rule under Robinson CQ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower and upper directional epiderivatives of a smooth-convex composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:X\to Y\) be continuously differentiable and let \(f:Y\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be lower semicontinuous and convex, with \(f(y_0)<+\infty\) for \(y_0=G(x_0)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implication and Equivalence Forms of Robinson Constraint Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationships among Robinson constraint qualification and tangent-cone, normal-cone, and radial-cone conditions under the standing constraint-system assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A:=DG(x_0)X-\mathcal R_K(G(x_0))\). Then
\[
\operatorname{RCQ}(x_0)\Rightarrow DG(x_0)X-T_K(G(x_0))=Y
\Rightarrow [DG(x_0)X]^\perp\cap N_K(G(x_0))=\{0\},
\]
and
\[
[DG(x_0)X]^\perp\cap N_K(G(x_0))=\{0\}
\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{cl}[DG(x_0)X-T_K(G(x_0))]=Y
\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{cl}\mathcal A=Y.
\]
If \(\operatorname{ri}\mathcal A\neq\varnothing\), these four conditions and \(\operatorname{RCQ}(x_0)\) are mutually equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robinson constraint qualification implies tangent-cone surjectivity, which implies the dual normal-cone condition. The dual condition is equivalent to the two closure-density conditions. If the radial-cone difference set has nonempty relative interior, all these conditions are equivalent to Robinson constraint qualification.
assumptions_latex: \text{The standing differentiable constraint-system assumptions for Robinson constraint qualification hold.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{RCQ}(x_0)\Rightarrow(2.182)\Rightarrow(2.183)\Longleftrightarrow(2.184)\Longleftrightarrow(2.185),\qquad \operatorname{ri}\mathcal A\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow \operatorname{RCQ}(x_0)\Longleftrightarrow(2.182)\Longleftrightarrow(2.183)\Longleftrightarrow(2.184)\Longleftrightarrow(2.185).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-order mutual approximation of a feasible set and its linearization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided first-order approximation for a smooth inverse-image constraint system under Robinson constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G:X\to Y\) be continuously differentiable at \(x_0\in\Phi:=G^{-1}(K)\), and suppose Robinson's constraint qualification holds. Define
\[
\mathcal T:=\{h\in X:DG(x_0)h\in T_K(G(x_0))\}.
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,\Phi)=o(\|x-x_0\|)\quad\text{for }x-x_0\in\mathcal T,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{dist}(h,\mathcal T)=o(\|h\|)\quad\text{for }x_0+h\in\Phi.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Robinson's constraint qualification, displacements satisfying the linearized constraint approach the feasible set with little-o relative error, while actual feasible displacements approach the linearized cone with little-o relative error.
assumptions_latex: G:X\to Y\text{ is continuously differentiable at }x_0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,\Phi)=o(\|x-x_0\|)\ \text{for }x-x_0\in\mathcal T,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(h,\mathcal T)=o(\|h\|)\ \text{for }x_0+h\in\Phi.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order expansion of the optimal value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric problems with equality and finitely many inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an o(\|u-u_0\|^2)-optimal solution \bar x(u) of (P_u) converges to x_0\in\mathcal S(u_0), f and G are twice continuously differentiable, Robinson's constraint qualification relative to K_0 holds, and the prescribed second-order conditions hold. Then, as d\to0,
\[

\]
where \mathcal S(PL_d) is the solution set of the corresponding linearized problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a quadratically accurate approximate solution, twice-continuous differentiability, strict Robinson qualification, and second-order conditions, the optimal value has a second-order expansion whose quadratic term is minimized over solutions of the linearized problem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product, Equality-Inequality, and Set-Constrained Forms of Robinson Qualification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent characterizations of Robinson constraint qualification for product constraints, equality–inequality systems, and an explicit convex set constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For product constraints with \(DG_1(x_0)\) onto and \(\operatorname{int}K_2\neq\varnothing\), RCQ is equivalent to the existence of \(h\in X\) such that
\[
G_1(x_0)+DG_1(x_0)h\in K_1,\qquad G_2(x_0)+DG_2(x_0)h\in\operatorname{int}K_2.
\]
If \(K_1=\{0\}\), surjectivity of \(DG_1(x_0)\) is necessary for RCQ, and RCQ is equivalent to
\[
DG_1(x_0)\text{ onto},\qquad 0\in\operatorname{int}\{G_2(x_0)+DG_2(x_0)[\ker DG_1(x_0)]-K_2\}.
\]
If additionally \(\operatorname{int}K_2\neq\varnothing\), the second condition is equivalently
\[
\exists h\in\ker DG_1(x_0):\ G_2(x_0)+DG_2(x_0)h\in\operatorname{int}K_2.
\]
For finitely many equality and inequality constraints, RCQ is equivalent to MFCQ: the equality gradients are linearly independent and there exists \(h\) annihilating them while satisfying \(Dg_i(x_0)h<0\) for every active inequality \(i\in I(x_0)\).
If \(Y_1=X\) and \(G_1(x)=x\), RCQ is equivalent to
\[
0\in\operatorname{int}\{G_2(x_0)+DG_2(x_0)[K_1-x_0]-K_2\}.
\]
For \(\Phi=\{x\in Q:G(x)\in K\}\), with closed convex \(Q\subset X\), \(K\subset Y\), and \(x_0\in\Phi\), the regularity conditions under discussion are equivalent to each other and respectively to
\[
0\in\operatorname{int}\{G(x_0)+DG(x_0)(Q-x_0)-K\}
\]
and
\[
DG(x_0)\mathcal R_Q(x_0)-\mathcal R_K(G(x_0))=Y.
\]
If \(\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing\), RCQ is also equivalent to
\[
\exists x'\in Q:\ G(x_0)+DG(x_0)(x'-x_0)\in\operatorname{int}K.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The corollary gives equivalent feasible-direction and interior formulations of Robinson qualification for product constraints. With an equality first component, surjectivity is necessary and feasible directions may be restricted to its derivative kernel. For finite equality–inequality systems this becomes MFCQ. It also gives reduced and radial-cone formulations for constraints consisting of membership in a closed convex set together with a mapped closed convex constraint.
assumptions_latex: \text{Product-form branches use the assumptions stated for }DG_1(x_0),K_1,K_2
\Phi=\{x\in Q:G(x)\in K\},\quad Q\subset X,\ K\subset Y\text{ closed and convex},\quad x_0\in\Phi
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{RCQ has the product-form, equality-kernel, MFCQ, set-constrained interior, radial-cone, and linearized Slater characterizations displayed above under their stated branch assumptions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Feasibility Correction under Directional Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local correction estimate for nearly feasible paths and realization of linearized feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume G is C^{1,1}, x_0\in\Phi(u_0), directional regularity holds at x_0 in direction d, and u(t)=u_0+td+o(t). If x:\mathbb R_+\to X satisfies \|x(t)-x_0\|\le\gamma\sqrt t and \operatorname{dist}(G(x(t),u(t)),K)\le\delta t for all sufficiently small t\ge0, then, for sufficiently small positive \gamma and \delta, there exist \bar x:\mathbb R_+\to X and c\ge0 such that G(\bar x(t),u(t))\in K and
\[\|\bar x(t)-x(t)\|\le c\left(1+t^{-1}\|x(t)-x_0\|\right)\operatorname{dist}(G(x(t),u(t)),K)\]
for all sufficiently small t\ge0. Moreover, every h satisfying the linearized feasibility condition (4.10) is a first-order feasible direction relative to d.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a C1,1 constraint mapping satisfying directional regularity, a path that stays within order square-root t of x0 and violates the constraint by at most order t can, when the two constants are sufficiently small, be corrected to a feasible path with the stated residual-dependent error bound. Every direction satisfying the referenced linearized condition is also realizable as a first-order feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar x,c\ge0:\ G(\bar x(t),u(t))\in K,\quad \|\bar x(t)-x(t)\|\le c\left(1+t^{-1}\|x(t)-x_0\|\right)\operatorname{dist}(G(x(t),u(t)),K)\quad\text{for small }t\ge0;\qquad h\text{ satisfying (4.10)}\Rightarrow h\text{ is first-order feasible relative to }d.
